etapes: Make a smooth dough by rubbing the flour and the butter, cut into pieces, together with your fingertips.
Moisten with 1/2 glass of lightly salted water.
Shape into a ball, leave to rest for 30 min and roll out the pastry on a sheet of ovenproof paper.

gateau-erika-chocolat-blanc-et-fruits-ro.titre: Erika's white chocolate and red berry cake

etapes: Line the tin, prick the pastry and bake at 180° for 15 to 18 min. Take out of the oven and leave to cool.
Break the chocolate into pieces, pour in the crème fraîche, heat in the microwave for 1 min.
Add half the fruit to the melted chocolate and stir, crushing them slightly so that the juice blends a little with the chocolate.
Pour this mixture into the tin, arrange the rest of the red berries on top, pressing them halfway into the chocolate.
Leave to cool in the fridge for at least 5 h.
Cut the rhubarb into small pieces (after peeling it), sauté it in a frying pan with a knob of butter, add the honey and cook for a further 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven on the 'tart' setting to 200°.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs with the sugars, add the cream and the flour, mix well.
Put the pastry (sweet shortcrust or puff) in the tart tin and prick the base and sides with a fork.
Place the rhubarb on the tart base, then pour the cream over it and bake for about 35’.

notes: Suggestion: you can add a diced banana.

etapes: Mix the softened butter and the sugar with a spatula.
Add the ground almonds, keep mixing well.
Add the eggs, mix with the electric mixer.
Spread this cream over the shortcrust pastry, then the pears.
Bake in 'eco' mode at 175° for 40’ on the 2nd shelf.

notes: Best eaten warm.

etapes: Blind-bake the shortcrust pastry for 10’, fan-assisted 200°, shelf 2.
Grate the zest of one lemon, squeeze the lemons.
In a bowl, vigorously mix the zest, the lemon juice, the egg yolk, the cream and the caster sugar. Adjust the sugar according to how tangy you want the tart to be.
Pour the mixture onto the pre-baked tart case. Bake for about 20’ on the 'tart' setting at 220°, shelf 2.
Beat the whites to stiff peaks, adding the icing sugar. Spread the whites over the slightly cooled tart (10’), making sure to go right to the edges (the meringue shrinks as it cools).
Return to the oven, fan-assisted 200°, shelf 2, for 10’.
Mix them with 100 g caster sugar, 1 sachet vanilla sugar, 1 tsp starch, 37.5 cl milk.
Cook over a low heat without boiling until thickened.
Make a shortcrust pastry with a little sugar, leave it to rest.
Meanwhile, put the washed and pitted cherries in a large saucepan, add the caster sugar, place over a medium heat and add the Maïzena dissolved in very little water.
Let the whole thing thicken for 20’, stirring regularly.
At the end of cooking, add the kirsch.
Roll out the pastry in a tart dish, either buttered or lined with baking paper, and prick the pastry all over with a fork.
Pour the cherry compote onto the pastry, smoothing the surface, and sprinkle with the granulated sugar.
Put in an oven preheated on combined heat to 210° on the first shelf and bake for about 45’, keeping an eye on it.
Turn out once cooled.

ingredients: 1 kg cooking apples (made into compote, 15 % sugar)
etapes: Peel the apples, cut them into quarters and cook them for 20 min with ½ glass of water and 15 % sugar. Mash them roughly with a fork and leave them to cool.

Make a smooth dough by rubbing the flour and the butter, cut into pieces, together with your fingertips. Moisten with 1/2 glass of lightly salted water. Shape into a ball, leave to rest for 30 min and roll out the pastry on a sheet of ovenproof paper.
Place the paper and pastry in the dish, fold in the excess pastry, trim off the excess paper. Prick the pastry, spread the compote over it.
Lay slices of small apples on top, cut evenly (peeled, of course).
Bake in the oven (rack on the top shelf) for 45 to 50 minutes, at 180° for 30 min, then fan-assisted at 210 for 16 min; check that it is nicely golden.
Take the tart out of the oven and sprinkle it with the rest of the sugar.

tarte-des-demoiselles-tatin.titre: Tarte des demoiselles Tatin (the Tatin sisters' tart)

ingredients: 200 g caster sugar for the caramel
etapes: Prepare the pastry by working the flour with 100 g butter cut into pieces, moistened with ½ glass of salted water; shape into a ball.
Roll out the pastry into a disc slightly larger than the diameter of the dish.
Remove the centre of the apples (core, pips) with an apple corer. Peel them.

Make a dark caramel. Arrange the whole apples (or halves, packed tightly) on the warm caramel. Cook for about ten minutes over a high heat. This way the apples will start to cook and will be well soaked in caramel.
Lay the pastry over the apples, press down a little to get a nice flat top.
Bake in the oven (rack at the bottom) for 45 minutes until the pastry is nicely golden.
Take the tart out of the oven and turn it out before it has completely cooled.

notes: Serve warm.

etapes: Prick the pastry with a fork.
Peel the apples, cut them into thin slices, arrange them on the pastry.
Put the flour and the sugar in a mixing bowl. Mix, make a well, add the whole eggs and the yolks. Mix with a wooden spoon, thinning it by adding the milk.
Pour this custard over the apples and bake for 30’ in a moderate oven, on the bottom shelf.
Peel the apples, slice them, arrange them on the pastry.
In a bowl, beat the whole eggs and the sugar. Add the Maïzena, the milk and lastly the calvados.
Pour the mixture over the apples, sprinkle with flaked almonds and put in a hot oven, on the oven floor. Oven at 200° for 45 min.
Pour the crème fraîche onto an unbaked shortcrust pastry base and arrange the apples, cut into quarters, on top.
Pour the following mixture over them: the sugar, the whole eggs, the melted butter, the flour, 1 tbsp calvados.
Put in a hot oven, 190 °C fan, shelf 1, for 45’.
Ten minutes before the end of cooking, add the almonds.
Preheat the oven, fan-assisted, to 180°.
Separate the whites from the yolks and whisk the egg whites with a pinch of salt to very stiff peaks.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar until the mixture turns pale.
Add the warm milk, the melted butter, the flour and the baking powder.
Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the batter.
Pour the batter into a previously buttered ring mould.
Put in the oven and bake for 25 minutes, then turn out immediately.
Make the hot syrup with the water, the cane sugar syrup and the rum, and soak the baba with it until fully absorbed.

notes: Serve chilled with a fruit salad and/or Chantilly cream.

etapes: Mix the sugar, the whole eggs, the rum, the flour and a sachet of baking powder.
Melt the butter very gently and pour it over the batter.
Add the chestnut cream to the batter, stirring well with the spoon.
Use the electric mixer. The batter takes on a 'marron glacé' colour.
Generously butter a round cake tin; pour in the batter and bake for 50 min at 180°.
Soften the butter and mix it with the chestnut cream; in another bowl, mix the egg yolks with the flour and the salt, then combine the 2 mixtures.
Whisk the egg whites to very stiff peaks and gently fold them into the previous mixture.
Pour the mixture into a buttered and floured round cake tin.
Bake for 45’ at 170° in a preheated oven.
Proceed as for variation a: gently fold in the beaten egg whites last.

ingredients: 30 g cream of rice or Maïzena
etapes: Melt the chocolate with the butter and 2 tbsp water in the microwave, about 2 min at power 350, stirring from time to time.
In a mixing bowl, mix the Maïzena with the ground almonds, the sugar and the egg yolks. Pour the melted chocolate and butter mixture over this batter and stir until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in gently so as not to knock the air out of them.
Pour into a Teflon tin and put in an oven preheated to 200° fan-assisted for 30 to 40 minutes.
Dust with icing sugar (using a stencil to decorate).

notes: Eat warm or cold, with crème anglaise or on its own.

etapes: Preheat the oven to 170°.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until pale.
Add the flour, the Maïzena and the baking powder, mix well.
Melt the chocolate with the butter, either in the microwave or in the oven.
Fold in the melted butter and chocolate mixture.
Pour the mixture into a buttered round cake tin.
Bake for 20’.
First, crack the walnuts and blanch them in boiling water to remove the skins.
Peel the apples and cut them into small dice.
Once that is done, switch the oven on to conventional + fan heat at 195°.
Beat the eggs with the sugar until pale.
Stir in the crème fraîche, then the roughly chopped walnuts and finally the flour and baking powder; whisk to obtain a smooth, even batter.
Fold in the apples.
Pour everything into a well-buttered round cake tin.
Decorate with a few walnut halves.
Bake on the first shelf for about 40 to 50’.
Leave to cool before turning out.
Peel the apples and keep them in water so they don't turn brown.
Beat the eggs with the sugar until pale, then add the vanilla sugar.
Stir in the melted butter, then the flour and baking powder, and mix with the electric mixer to obtain a smooth batter; stir in the rum.
Cut the apples into small cubes and fold them into the batter.
Pour the mixture into a generously buttered tin.
Meanwhile, switch the oven on to fan at 145°.
Put in the oven on the 2nd shelf and bake for 40’; to finish, raise the temperature to 160° for 15’, keeping an eye on it.
Leave to cool in the tin before turning out.

notes: Variation: first fry the peeled and cut apples in butter in a frying pan to caramelise them.

etapes: Butter a round cake tin and sprinkle it with sugar to coat it.
Beat the eggs, add the rest of the sugar and the rest of the softened butter, the pinch of salt, the flour and the Maïzena, then the baking powder.
Arrange the mirabelles in the tin.
Pour the batter over the mirabelles.
Bake in an oven preheated to 180° fan-assisted for 35’.

notes: Serve warm on its own or with crème fraîche or a scoop of vanilla ice cream, or cold.

etapes: Peel the pears, cut them into quarters and poach them for 15 min in a syrup made with ¼ litre of water and 70 g caster sugar.
Bring the milk to the boil with 50 g sugar and the sachet of vanilla sugar. Sprinkle in the semolina and stir throughout the cooking time: 8 min.
Off the heat, stir in the egg yolk.
Pour the semolina into a buttered tin, lay the pear quarters on top and sprinkle with the ground almonds.
Put in the oven fan-assisted at 220° for 10 min. Let it brown a little.

notes: Serve hot with the pear poaching syrup in a sauce boat, but it can also be eaten cold.

gateau-de-savoie-a-lancienne.titre: Old-fashioned gâteau de Savoie (Savoy sponge cake)

ingredients: 150 g sugar with a sachet of vanilla sugar
etapes: Separate the egg whites and whisk them to very stiff peaks.
Whisk the yolks with the salt and the sugar until pale, then add the flour and the starch and work everything together to obtain a smooth batter.
Fold in a little of the egg white to loosen the batter slightly, then gently fold in the rest of the whites, lifting the batter, to obtain a batter that is both light and firm.
Pour the batter into a buttered and sugared round cake tin, 26 cm in diameter.
Put in an oven preheated to 190° in eco mode on the 2nd shelf for 40’.
Turn out immediately upside down onto a wire rack.
Melt the butter in the microwave and leave it to cool.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and the sugar until pale.
Add the flour while beating, then the butter and the milk to obtain a very smooth batter.
Wash and pit the apricots, cut them in half.
Butter a round cake tin, place the apricot halves in it rounded side up and sprinkle them with the sachet of vanilla sugar.
Put in an oven preheated on combined heat to 200° on the 2nd shelf.
Bake for 45’.

notes: Eat warm or cold.

etapes: Boil the apricots with the water and 1 glass of rum for 25 min.
Beat the eggs with the caster sugar until pale.
Add the salt and the flour, then the milk, the vanilla sugar and the 2nd glass of rum, beating to obtain a very smooth mixture.
Preheat the oven to 150° fan.
Drain the apricots and cut them into small pieces, then dust them with flour.
Pour the batter into the buttered tin, then spread the apricots over it.
Bake on shelf no. 2 at 150° for 1 hour.
Then, on shelf no. 3, raise the temperature and finish cooking at 230° for another 3 min.

ingredients: 40 g lightly salted butter + 20 g for the tin
etapes: Preheat the oven to 210° (gas mark 7).
Melt the 40 g of butter; mix the flour, the sugar, the salt and the vanilla sugar.
Add the eggs gradually, then the milk little by little, still mixing.
Add the melted butter.
Butter the round cake tin generously.
Place the cherries in the tin, then pour over the runny batter.
Bake for 5’ at 210°, then lower to 180° and bake for another 40’ + 10’ with the oven switched off.

notes: Serve the clafoutis still warm or cold, dusted with icing sugar.

etapes: Preheat the oven, fan-assisted, to 210°.
Wash and pit the mirabelles, then place them in a well-buttered tin.
With the electric mixer, mix the eggs, the sugar, the pinch of salt, the flour, the melted butter and finally the milk to obtain a very smooth batter.
Cover the mirabelles with this batter.
Bake at 210° for 15 minutes, then lower the temperature to 150° for 30 minutes.

notes: Serve warm or cold.

etapes: Peel and slice the pears and arrange them on the base of a 26 cm round tin.
Beat the eggs with the sugar and the vanilla sugar, add half the milk and the cream, then the Maïzena, first dissolved in the other half of the milk, and the salt.
Beat again to obtain a very smooth but not frothy batter.
Pour the mixture over the pears.
Bake in an oven preheated to 210° fan-assisted for 35 to 40 minutes.

ingredients: 375 g plums (greengages), peeled, pitted and halved
Butter for the tin and the top of the batter
etapes: Make a well with the flour in a mixing bowl, add the eggs, the sugar and a pinch of salt, and whisk, gradually drawing in the flour; slowly thin the mixture by adding the milk and finish by stirring in the melted butter. Work everything carefully to obtain a supple, smooth batter.
Butter a sufficiently deep tart tin, arrange the fruit, pour the batter over the fruit, dot the surface with a few small knobs of butter and sprinkle with the sachet of vanilla sugar.
Bake in a hot oven, fan-assisted at 220°, for 30 min.

notes: Serve warm or cold.
N.B.: the fruit can be cherries, apricots, grapes…

ingredients: 250 g pitted prunes (soaked for about 1/4 hour, then floured)
etapes: Beat the sugar and the whole eggs with the electric mixer for 5 minutes until the mixture turns pale.
Add the salt, the melted butter, the flour and the milk, mix with the electric mixer.
Add the rum and the prunes.
Put into a buttered dish in a preheated oven.
Conventional heat at 200° for 20 minutes on shelf 2, then 20’ at 180°. Leave for 5’ in the closed, switched-off oven.
Make the batter as follows: beat the sugar and the vanilla sugar with the eggs until pale. Add the flour, then the milk, still using the electric mixer. Add the rum.
Leave the batter to rest for 1 h in the fridge.
Preheat the oven, fan-assisted, to 200°.
Generously butter a heavy dish, spreading the fat well over the base and sides.
Pour the batter into the dish; add the prunes, first rolled in flour so they don't sink to the bottom.
Bake for ½ hour on the 2nd shelf at 200°. Then switch off the oven and leave for another ½ h.

notes: Important: once the dish is in the oven, do not open the oven door for an hour.

etapes: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Butter an ovenproof dish. Drain the pears and place them in the bottom of the dish.
Beat the whole eggs with the caster sugar in a mixing bowl. Add the flour, then gradually pour in the whole milk, mixing well, until you have a lump-free custard.
Pour the custard over the pears in the dish. Leave to rest for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place the dish in a large deep tray filled with water.
Bake in the bain-marie for 30 minutes.
When it comes out of the oven, let the pear flan cool slightly on a wire rack.
Serve the pear flan warm, preferably, or cold, decorated with a dab of Chantilly cream.
Peel the pears. Slice them thinly. Butter a dish and arrange the pears in it in an even layer.
Heat the milk with the butter.
Mix the flour, the salt, the vanilla sugar and 75 g caster sugar.
Add the whole eggs one by one, then the milk little by little and finally the rum.
Pour over the pears. Sprinkle with the rest of the sugar.
To finish, bake at 220 °C for 25 to 30’.
Line a tart tin with the puff pastry, then prick it with a fork.
Heat the milk with part of the sugar until it comes to the boil.

Meanwhile, whisk together the rest of the sugar and the Maïzena or flour. In another container, large enough to hold the milk, beat the eggs with a little hot milk, add the sugar and Maïzena mixture and whisk well to avoid lumps.
Pour the boiling milk over this mixture while whisking vigorously, put it into the saucepan and bring the custard to the boil for 3 minutes, whisking constantly.
Pour the custard into the tin, leave to cool for 30 minutes and bake in an oven preheated to 210/230°. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.

ingredients: 110 g cane or white caster sugar
etapes: Bring the milk to the boil.
Whisk the eggs, the sugar and the sachets of vanilla sugar until pale.
Add the Maïzena dissolved in a little milk, then pour in the boiling milk, still whisking.
Return to the saucepan and start cooking over a low heat, stirring constantly for 10 minutes.
Pour into a buttered tin and put in an oven preheated, fan-assisted, to 180°.
Bake on the 2nd shelf for 45’, then leave in the switched-off oven for another 15’ without opening the door.
Leave to cool, turn out and serve with caramel (optional).
Bring the milk to the boil with the sugar and the vanilla sugar, set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180° fan.
Beat the eggs and slowly pour the milk over the beaten eggs, stirring with a wooden spoon.
Put a sheet of kitchen paper on the bottom of the dish and arrange the ramekins on it.
Pour the custard into the ramekins.
Put the dish in the oven (shelf no. 2).
Pour the water for the bain-marie into the dish to halfway up.
Bake at 180° for 40’.
Take out of the oven and leave to cool.

ingredients: 2 tbsp cassonade or soft brown sugar
etapes: Brown the bananas in butter in a frying pan for 8’, then pour the orange juice over them.
Leave to simmer for a few seconds, then add the cassonade, pour in the rum, flambé and serve.

crottin-de-chevre-sur-pommes-poelees-au-.titre: Goat's cheese crottin on honey-fried apples

etapes: Cut the apples into quarters, remove the core and cut into thin wedges.
Roughly chop the pistachios.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, then brown the apple wedges on both sides; season with pepper and drizzle with honey.
Spread the golden apples in a dish, place 8 slices of goat's cheese on top and sprinkle with pistachios.
Put under the oven grill for 2 minutes.
Garnish with chives and serve immediately.
Peel the apples and slice them.
Brown them in the butter.
Add the cane sugar and the calvados.
Flambé.
Serve and enjoy.

ingredients: 1 sachet of brioche yeast or 2 sachets of baker's yeast
For glazing: a little milk or a beaten egg
etapes: Mix the flour, sugar and salt, and make a well. Add the yeast, slowly pour in the lukewarm milk, the beaten egg and the melted butter*.
Knead with the mixer fitted with the right attachment.
Cover and leave to rest for 30 min at 25°.
On a floured work surface, shape 4 very smooth balls, place them in a well-greased loaf tin and cover with a cloth. Leave to rise in a warm place for 1 h.
Brush the dough with the milk or beaten egg and put it in an oven at 180°.
Bake for 25 min (oven on the low position); the brioche should be nicely golden; cover with a sheet of foil if it browns too much.

notes: Note 1: * For the butter, I prefer to cut the butter into the milk and warm everything for 40 s in the microwave.
Note 2: to make the dough rise (25°), if the room temperature is too low, use the oven at 25°, and after the last rise bake for 35 min at 180°.
Note 3: in the photo, the tin is too short.

etapes: In a saucepan, melt a knob of butter.
Add the rice and heat over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in the whole milk, then the sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir and turn down the heat.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 35 minutes. Check the consistency: the milk should be creamy and the rice well cooked.
Pour into a mould whose base is coated with liquid caramel, and leave to cool.

notes: Serve with liquid caramel poured over each portion.

etapes: Peel the apples and cut them into 8.
Heat half the butter in a Teflon frying pan and brown the apples in it, turning them and sprinkling them with 2 tbsp of sugar halfway through. Keep warm.

Make a soufflé omelette: separate the whites from the yolks, whisk the whites to very stiff peaks with a pinch of salt, beat the yolks with 2 tbsp of sugar and the sachet of vanilla sugar. When the mixture turns pale, gently fold in the beaten whites.
Cook the omelette with the rest of the butter in a large stainless-steel frying pan, turning it halfway through, uncovered.
Cover half of the omelette with the apples, fold the other half over and slide onto the stainless-steel serving dish.
Heat the calvados in a small saucepan, set it alight, pour it over the omelette, present and serve at once.
In a saucepan, melt a knob of butter.
Add the rice and heat over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in the whole milk, then the sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir and turn down the heat.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 35 minutes. Check the consistency: the milk should be creamy and the rice well cooked.

vin-chaud.intro: Difficulty: easy. Preparation time: 5 minutes. Cooking time: 15 minutes.

etapes: Gently heat 1 l of good red wine to which you have added 1 lemon cut into quarters, a split vanilla pod, the zest of an orange and the sugar.
Keep it just below the boil for 15 min, strain and serve piping hot.

notes: In moderation.

A wonderful stimulant, cinnamon warms you up and fights germs. If you catch a chill or feel the flu coming on, make mulled wine by putting two large glasses of a full-bodied wine in a saucepan. Add a cinnamon stick broken into small pieces, four cloves and two tablespoons of cane sugar. Bring to the boil, then simmer over low heat for six to eight minutes. Shortly before the end, add the juice of half a lemon, strain and serve very hot.

etapes: Peel the avocado, remove the stone and cut it into cubes.
Remove the grapefruit rind, peel it and cut into small pieces.
Peel the shallot and chop it very finely, make a vinaigrette and mix everything together; keep in the fridge.
The prawns are added just before serving.

notes: The dish can be prepared the day before.

ingredients: Freshly ground pepper: a few turns
etapes: Remove the stalks from the spinach and wash it in cold water, blanch it for 3 min in salted water, and cook it for 10 min in the pressure cooker.
In the sauté pan: melt the butter over medium heat. Add the pine nuts and the finely chopped garlic. Let them colour very lightly for 2 or 3 minutes.
Add the crème fraîche and stir. Add the spinach and stir gently. Keep over low heat, covered, for about 5 minutes.
Season with pepper and sprinkle with freshly grated nutmeg. It's ready!

notes: Serve with an omelette.

ingredients: One medium pattypan squash or two small ones
etapes: Cook the whole squash (or squashes) in boiling salted water for 15 min, drain and leave to cool.
Meanwhile, slice the onion and fry it for 5 min in a saucepan with oil.
Add the (minced) meat, pepper and thyme. Simmer over low heat while you prepare the squash.
Cut off the top and carefully hollow out the squash. Keep the flesh, dice it and add it to the saucepan. Add some cornflour mixed with water and let it thicken.
Off the heat, add the grated Comté and salt if needed.
Preheat the oven to 170°.
Fill the squash with this stuffing and put the top back on. Place in an oiled baking dish, drizzle each squash with olive oil and sprinkle with a pinch of thyme, and bake for 25 min.

notes: Note about this recipe (first try):
Even with a medium squash, the skin stays too tough! So it is much better to use small pattypan squashes, if only for the presentation.
You need enough cornflour to thicken the stuffing properly.
With a medium or large squash, I think it's better to remove all the flesh and make a simple gratin! Apart from that, it was good!!
With 2, more is much better!

pommes-de-terre-en-salade.intro: In the photo: with smoked herrings and with smoked trout.

etapes: Preparing the potatoes: steam the potatoes for 12 min. Before peeling them, check (by pricking them with a knife) that they are cooked through.
Peel them while hot, as they absorb the dressing much better; cut them into cubes. Add them to the dressing.
For the dressing: 3 tablespoons of vinegar + 1 of water and 1 of mustard, salt, pepper, parsley, finely chopped garlic. Mix, then 3 spoonfuls of oil, mix. The dressing is ready.
Add the potatoes.

notes: Note 1: for tuna, use tinned tuna in olive oil, and use the oil for the dressing (more flavour).
Note 2: but of course you can use cooked meat: chicken breast, pork, ham in cubes or not, cooked or smoked, cooked bacon lardons, smoked trout or salmon, prawns, mussels, etc.
The salad can be enriched with sliced radishes, lettuce, beetroot, peas, etc.

etapes: Wash the courgettes and the aubergine and cut them into medium-sized cubes (red and green pepper too, for those who like it). Cut the tomatoes into quarters and slice the onion.

In a pressure cooker, pour a good tablespoon of olive oil and fry the different vegetables one after the other for 5 minutes so they colour. Start with the peppers, then the aubergines, the courgettes and finally the onions, and finish with the tomatoes.
Mix everything together, season with salt and pepper, add the crushed garlic and the bouquet garni, then cover and cook for 15 minutes once the steam starts.
Before serving, don't hesitate to taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Peel the Jerusalem artichokes, rinse them and cut them into thin slices.
In a saucepan, cover with salted water. Cook in boiling water for 30 min. Check they are done, drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the thick crème fraîche. Season generously with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Pour this cream over the Jerusalem artichokes and mix. Enjoy the creamed Jerusalem artichokes piping hot on warm plates.

notes: In the photo, they are served with a beef burger patty, but any red meat (rib steak, beef steak, duck breast) works.

etapes: Peel and wash the potatoes and cut them into thin slices: do not wash them after slicing, as the starch is needed for the right consistency.

In a saucepan, bring the milk, crushed garlic, salt, pepper and nutmeg to the boil, then add the potatoes and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, depending on how firm they are (once it comes back to the boil, turn the heat down to 5). Stir from time to time so they don't stick to the bottom of the pan.
Rub a gratin dish with the butter. Arrange the drained potatoes in the dish, cover them with the cream, then dot small knobs of butter on top.
Bake for 50 min to 1 hour. Bake with fan heat only, 180°, 2nd shelf.

notes: Serve with Bayonne ham, 2 slices per person.

etapes: Cook the chard for 10 minutes in the pressure cooker.

Fry the sliced onions in the butter until translucent. Add the crushed tomatoes and the chopped garlic. Season with salt and pepper and leave to thicken for 30 minutes over low heat. Add the chopped chard.
Preheat the oven to 200° (gas mark 6-7).
Generously butter a gratin dish, pour in the mixture, sprinkle with Gruyère and bake for 30 minutes.
Cook the bulgur for 10 minutes in boiling salted water, drain and leave to cool a little.
Slice the onion and courgettes into rounds and fry them in a sauté pan with butter, covered, until cooked (15 minutes).
Off the heat, mix them with the cream (don't drain them too much), season with salt and pepper and spice with nutmeg.
Beat the eggs with the milk, add 100 g of Gruyère, and stir everything into the bulgur.
In an ovenproof dish, arrange in successive layers: the bulgur mixture, the vegetable mixture, finishing with the remaining 50 g of Gruyère.
Bake for 30 min with fan heat at 220° (preheated oven).

notes: Suggestions: add 2 tbsp of tomato purée, or replace the courgettes with vegetables or minced meat of your choice.
Can be eaten cold.

ingredients: Tartare: one tub (for the recipe as made: 4 small garlic cheeses)
etapes: Grate the carrots and cook them for 10 min.
Fry the sliced onion. Add the carrots, as well as the surimi cut into small pieces, the scallops and the prawns.
Mix everything with the crème fraîche and the cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour everything into an ovenproof dish, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and bake for 20 min at 220°.

notes: Ingredients suggested by the recipe.

etapes: Clean, cut into small dice (because of the fibres) and cook for 10 min; drain.
Mix the dice and the crème fraîche in a large bowl, season with salt and pepper.
Spread the mixture in an ovenproof dish. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake for about 4-5 minutes with the oven on grill, until the gratin is nicely golden.
Serve very hot, sprinkled with snipped herbs.
Steam the cauliflower in florets, 10' on setting 2 in the pressure cooker.
Make a Mornay sauce with the sauce maker (without a sauce maker, see note).
Mash the cauliflower into a purée, stir in the Mornay sauce, add the ham cut into strips, the chopped chervil (optional), 50 g of butter and the Gruyère.
Pour into a dish and brown in the oven for 10 min.

parties.nom: White sauce (note: without a sauce maker)
etapes: In a saucepan, melt the butter; when it starts to sizzle, add the flour all at once and whisk well.
Once the mixture is smooth, add the cold milk all at once. Mix well and bring to the boil. The béchamel sauce will start to thicken.
Season with fine salt, pepper and grated nutmeg.
Add an egg yolk (not essential), mix and cook for a few minutes, stirring constantly. Add the grated Gruyère.
Wash the courgettes without peeling them, wipe them dry and cut them into 1 cm thick slices.
Drop them into 3 litres of boiling salted water and cook for 15 minutes (in the pressure cooker, 5 min after dropping them into the boiling water).
Tip them into a colander to drain, and press them with the skimmer to squeeze out the excess water.
Put the courgettes into a buttered ovenproof dish and roughly mash them with a fork.
In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs as for an omelette, add the cream and the grated Gruyère, season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with grated nutmeg.
Pour this mixture over the courgettes, mix, and brown in a hot oven (180°) for 15 min.

notes: Note: same recipe with pattypan squash.

etapes: Butter an ovenproof gratin dish. Chop the shallots. Shell the pistachios.

Peel and wash the potatoes. Cut them into thin slices. Cut the squash in half, scoop out the seeds and cut one half into thin slices (the rest can be used for a purée with potato). Cut the ham into strips.

In the gratin dish, spread the chopped shallots, arrange a layer of potatoes, a layer of ham, a layer of squash, season with salt and pepper, add nutmeg, scatter with pistachios and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Fill the gratin dish this way, alternating the ingredients. Finish with a layer of squash. Pour over the single cream and sprinkle with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake at 180° for 45 min to 1 h, until the tip of a knife goes in easily and the top is nicely golden.
Roll the shortcrust pastry into a buttered tin and preheat your oven to gas mark 7 (210°).
Wash the endives, cut them into rounds and fry them in a frying pan with the butter for 10 min.
In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs with the cream, and add salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Remove the rind around the edge of the Camembert, cut it into slices and arrange it on the pastry. Then add the endives and the egg and cream mixture.
Bake for 30 min.
Make a shortcrust pastry by working the flour with the softened butter in pieces, then half a glass of salted water.
Roll out the pastry with a rolling pin and lay it in a buttered, lightly floured tart dish. Prick the pastry with a fork.
In a bowl, with the mixer, beat the eggs as for an omelette, add the cream, the grated cheese and the small pinch of salt.
Arrange the bacon, cut into dice or strips, on the pastry, pour the filling over it and bake in an oven preheated on the pastry setting at 220° for 30 min.

notes: Serve with an endive salad dressed with olive oil, with slices of apple and walnut halves.

etapes: Make a shortcrust pastry or use a shop-bought all-butter one, line a tart dish with it and prick the pastry all over with a fork.
Brown the lardons in a non-stick frying pan.
In a jug, break the whole eggs, add a little salt and pepper, add the crème fraîche and whisk everything together, then add the Gruyère, the drained lardons and the diced pork shoulder.
Spread the mixture over the pastry.
Bake in an oven preheated on eco at 210° on the 2nd shelf for 40', then turn out.

notes: Serve with a salad.

etapes: Lay the shortcrust pastry in a tart tin. Prick the base with a fork and blind-bake for 15 min (oven preheated to 180 °C). Take the pastry out of the oven and set aside.

Peel the Jerusalem artichokes and chop them roughly. Put them in a saucepan, cover with water and add salt. Cook for 30 min, until the Jerusalem artichokes are very tender. Drain them and put them in a mixing bowl. Add the crème fraîche and mash to a purée. Season with salt and pepper.

Spread the mustard over the tart base. Spread the Jerusalem artichoke purée evenly. Sprinkle with grated Emmental. Bake for 15 min (at 180 °C). When the Jerusalem artichoke tart is nicely golden, take it out of the oven and enjoy immediately.
Finely slice the leek whites and the shallot and soften them in a sauté pan with the butter, covered, over low heat for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle in 1 tbsp of flour, stir gently, then add the milk and cream and simmer for 10 minutes; season with salt and pepper and add the nutmeg.
Meanwhile, fry the lardons in a frying pan, then add them to the mixture. Remove from the heat and add the 2 previously beaten eggs. Then leave to cool completely.
Preheat the oven with fan heat to 200°.

Roll out the pastry into 2 circles, then line the tin, covered with baking paper, with the larger of the 2, letting a little pastry hang over. Fill the pastry with the cooled mixture, cover with the second circle of pastry, seal the edges well, and glaze the pastry with the beaten egg yolk.
Put in the oven and bake for 40 minutes; leave to cool or until lukewarm before serving.
Peel the potatoes, then cut them into thin slices.
Roll out 2/3 of the puff pastry and lay it in a tart tin, making sure it hangs over the edge by 2 cm.
Arrange layers of potatoes on the pastry, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Fold the overhanging pastry back over, then moisten it with a damp brush.
Roll out the remaining third of the pastry into a circle slightly smaller than the diameter of the tin. Place it on the moistened pastry edges. Press so the two pastries stick together.
Decorate with the pastry trimmings.
Make a chimney in the centre with aluminium foil.
Bake in a hot oven (210°, tart setting) for 25 min.
Once cooked, cut a lid in the top of the pie, then pour in the crème fraîche mixed with nutmeg. Put the lid back and return to the oven for 5 min.

notes: Serve with a green salad.

ingredients: 10 cl Jura white wine (Savagnin or a characterful Chardonnay)
etapes: Fondue: cut the Morbier into slices (put it in the freezer 30 min beforehand to make it easier to cut).

In a fondue pot, fry the garlic and shallot with a knob of butter. Add the white wine, heat it and stir in the slices of Morbier, a little salt, pepper, nutmeg and the starch, until you get a thick fondue.
Poach the artichoke bottoms in salted water (simmering water, 5 min), and poach the Montbéliard sausage in plain water (simmering water, 15 min).
Leave everything to cool. In an ovenproof dish, lay the artichoke bottoms, fill them with slices of Montbéliard sausage, and coat with the fondue.
Brown everything in the oven (gas mark 7 for 10 min).
Cook the potatoes in their skins in salted water.
Leave them to cool.
In a frying pan, brown the small lardons and an onion cut into thin slices, with a little butter (and the fat from the lardons). Set aside.
In the frying pan, brown the potatoes, peeled and cut into slices.
In a rectangular earthenware dish, put a layer of potatoes, the lardons and onions, cover with the rest of the potatoes, and spread the fresh Cantal cut into small cubes on top.
Put in the oven for 20 min and let it brown.

notes: Serve with a salad and cured country ham.
Bon appétit!

etapes: 1 kg white potatoes boiled and well drained. Mash the potatoes.
In a non-stick frying pan, heat 100 g of crème fraîche, and melt in it 300 g of fresh tomme cut into pieces and a hint of garlic.
Mix everything over high heat and make it "stretch".
Adjust the seasoning; if needed, loosen with a little milk or water.

notes: Serve piping hot with salad and Auvergne ham.

etapes: Cook the potatoes for 14 min in the pressure cooker.
In another saucepan, cook the sausage for about twenty minutes if you're not going with the charcuterie option (but both can go together if there are a lot of guests).
Use the special container, or put the Mont d'Or lid under the box, then wrap the box in aluminium foil so it doesn't burn in the oven.
Dig a hole about 2 cm in diameter and add the chopped garlic and the white wine.
Put the cheese in the oven at 180-200 °C (gas mark 6-7) until melted, about 30 minutes.
Serve hot with the potatoes, the sausage (or charcuterie) and the lamb's lettuce.

notes: For more flavour: don't hesitate to pepper the cheese and potatoes just before eating.
Dry white wine.

etapes: In a saucepan over low heat, melt the butter, add the flour and mix quickly with a wooden spoon. Let the flour cook for a few seconds.
Off the heat, pour in the milk all at once, stir briskly and put the saucepan back on the heat. Stirring constantly, cook this mixture, which should be thick, for 10 min.
Season lightly with salt, add pepper and sprinkle with grated nutmeg. Leave to cool slightly.
Add the 5 egg yolks one at a time, then the grated Gruyère.
Whisk the whites to very stiff peaks and fold them in very gently, always lifting the mixture from underneath.
Butter a soufflé dish (18 to 20 cm in diameter) and pour the mixture into it.
With the oven switched on 15 min beforehand (rotisserie setting, 200°), put it in and bake for 40 min, keeping an eye on it.
Bring it to the table immediately: "a soufflé waits for no one".
Cook the potatoes in their skins in salted water (or 12 min in the pressure cooker). Leave them to cool, then peel them and cut them into slices.
In a frying pan, brown the small lardons and an onion cut into thin slices, with a little butter (and the fat from the lardons). Set aside.
In the frying pan, brown the peeled, sliced potatoes. Add the lardons and onions and the white wine, and simmer for 15 min before transferring everything to a gratin dish.
Scrape the Reblochon with a knife, cut it in half horizontally and lay it on the potatoes, rind side down.
Put in the oven (220°) for 20 to 30 min and let it brown.

notes: Serve with a salad and cured country ham.

etapes: Cut the endives into strips.
Peel and slice the onion.
In a frying pan, sweat the onion in 1 tbsp of olive oil over low heat.
When it starts to colour, add the endive strips and sauté everything for 3 min over high heat. Season lightly with salt and pepper and pour into an earthenware ovenproof dish.
Brown the lardons in the frying pan without any fat. Pour them over the endives and cover with slices of Reblochon.
Bake for 10 min in the (preheated) oven on the rotisserie setting at 210° on the 3rd shelf, then 3 min under the grill.

notes: Enjoy straight out of the oven, before the cheese sets.

etapes: Peel the potatoes, rinse them and grate them.
Cover them with water, then rinse them again. Drain them very well in a mixing bowl (use paper towels!).
Add the cornflour and some salt: mix.
Separately, beat the eggs as for an omelette, then pour them over the potatoes, stir well with a spatula and add the cheese (for those who like it, a finely chopped onion is a nice addition).
Pour the mixture into a non-stick frying pan brushed with oil.
Cook covered over very low heat (3-4) for 10 min, turn over and cook for another 8 min.
Serve.
Slice the onion.
Wash and peel the tomatoes and cut them into pieces.
In a casserole dish, heat the oil and brown the onions, then add the tomatoes, garlic, salt and pepper, mix and cook for 20 min over low heat.
In a small bowl, break the eggs and beat them as for an omelette or scramble them, add salt, add the tomatoes and mix well.
Pour everything into a large frying pan and cook for 2 to 4 min, stirring constantly.

notes: Serve with a salad.

etapes: Peel the onion and carrots. Slice the onion and cut the carrots into rounds.
In a saucepan, sweat the onion, carrots and peas.
Add the chicken stock and simmer for 30 min.
Put everything through the vegetable mill, and discard what's left of the pea pods in the mill (the hens love it!).
Put back on the heat for 10 min. Serve.

ingredients: 400 g pitted cherries per person (Gorge de pigeon type)
etapes: Wash and pit the cherries.
Cook them in a frying pan with 10 g butter for 15 min over medium heat. There should be almost no juice left. Set aside.
Brown the lamb chops for 3 min on each side, season with salt.
Serve on a warm plate.

ingredients: 2 tomatoes or 1 small can of tomato sauce
etapes: Peel the potatoes, tomatoes and onions, slice them thinly and spread them in a buttered baking dish. Pour 2 glasses of milk into the dish and bake in a medium oven (fan oven at 200°) for 30 min.

Meanwhile, finely chop two good pinches of rosemary and mix with 50 g butter seasoned with salt and pepper. Spread the inside of the meat with this mixture. Roll it up and tie it so that the flavoured butter is sealed inside. Brush the outside of the meat with oil. Stud the skin with sprigs of rosemary.

If the tomatoes are replaced by tomato sauce, pour it over the vegetables at the end of cooking and mix everything together. Place the shoulder on the vegetables, which should have absorbed almost all the milk.
Return to the oven (fan oven 220°) for 35 min, turning the meat at least twice.
Serve in the baking dish.

The day before, once boned and tied: make small cuts in the meat and slip in a few garlic cloves. Brush it with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Wrap it in cling film with the thyme and rosemary.
On the day: butter an ovenproof dish, slice the potatoes and onion thinly, then put them in the dish. Lay the lamb shoulder on the potatoes with the thyme and rosemary, add a glass of water.
Cook for at least 1h30 at 200°, turning the shoulder halfway through so that it is nicely browned all over.
The dish can wait for the guests in the oven… If the shoulder browns too much, cover with foil.

notes: In season, add 400 g of fine peeled beefsteak tomatoes when cooking; their juice will replace ½ glass of water.
Note, in a pressure cooker: brown the shoulder prepared the day before well on all 4 sides with the onion. Add the potatoes, peeled and halved, and cook for 35 minutes.

selle-dagneau-aux-haricots-blancs-et-tom.titre: Saddle of lamb with white beans and tomatoes

ingredients: 500 g fine tomatoes from the garden
Thyme, garlic, oil, salt and pepper
etapes: Prepare the beans in advance: cook them in a saucepan of water with a pinch of coarse salt for about 30 min, with salt and garlic. Same for the tomatoes, in a frying pan with the sliced shallot.

Lightly score the fat of the saddle of lamb, stud it with a few pieces of garlic, add a sprig of thyme and tie it, oil it, put it in a hot oven (200°, shelf 3) and let the saddle cook for 20 to 25 min.
Season with salt and pepper, add the beans around the meat along with the tomato, and cook for another 5 min.

paves-dautruche-sel-et-poivre-pommes-dau.titre: Salt-and-pepper ostrich steaks with pommes dauphines

etapes: Follow the defrosting instructions.
Sear over high heat for 2 min on each side in a frying pan with a little fat. Lower the heat and finish cooking for 4 min per side.
Serve with pommes dauphines or duchess potatoes, and a salad.

parties.nom: Variation: ostrich steaks with mustard (additional ingredients)
etapes: Pepper the ostrich steaks (preferably with five-berry pepper). In a mixture of oil and butter, sear the steaks over medium heat for 5 min on each side (cooked through), then set aside on plates kept warm in the oven.
Deglaze the pan with 2 tablespoons of crème fraîche and 2 tablespoons of wholegrain mustard. Season with salt and serve the steaks coated with the sauce, with pommes noisettes and a salad.
Steam the fennel bulbs, halved and with the green stalks removed. Sweat a thinly sliced onion and brown it in butter. Add the fennel and brown gently over low heat, set aside.
In a frying pan, with the oil as hot as possible, cook the meat for 30 s on each side.
Serve on warm plates.

ingredients: 250 g beef shin (left over from a pot-au-feu)
½ stock cube in 2 glasses of water
etapes: In the frying pan, brown the onion in the butter. Once golden brown, add the flour, let it colour lightly, then add the stock all at once, season with salt and pepper and cook for 12 min.
At the end of cooking, add the vinegar and the gherkins.

notes: As a variation: tomato and gherkin sauce.

joues-de-boeuf-confites-au-cidre.intro: Preparation: 30 min – Cooking: 3 h – Resting: 1 day.

etapes: Peel the carrots and cut them into small dice.
Peel the shallots and slice them.
Cut the beef cheeks into pieces. Marinate them with the cider, shallots, carrots and bouquet garni for 24 hours.
Peel the onions and slice them.
Drain the meat and vegetables, keeping the marinade.
Season the pieces of meat with salt and pepper.
Brown them in a casserole dish with the olive oil.
Fry the onions and lardons with the rest of the oil in the casserole dish.
Add the tomato purée and a pinch of sugar, and stir.
Return the meat to the pot, with the marinade and the beef stock.
Season with salt and pepper and adjust the seasoning. Cook for three hours over low heat.
Just before serving, sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve with homemade mashed potatoes.

paleron-de-boeuf-aux-carottes-et-a-l-ora.titre: Beef chuck with carrots and orange

ingredients: 1 capsule of veal stock (fond de veau)
etapes: Cut the meat into 4 portions.
Dissolve the veal stock in 1 bowl of boiling water.
Peel the carrots and cut them into thick sticks.

Heat the oil in the pressure cooker, sear the pieces of meat on all sides, fry the sliced onion, then pour in the orange juice. Add the carrots, garlic and veal stock, season with salt and pepper, add the thyme. Close and cook for 1 h.
Serve the meat and carrots on warm plates and keep warm. Add the butter to the meat's cooking juices. Whisk vigorously off the heat, then coat the meat with this sauce.
Serve immediately.
Peel the potatoes and cook them in salted water with the garlic. Mash, then add the Gruyère and the crème fraîche.
Preferably use leftover pot-au-feu, or cook the beef as a pot-au-feu.
Put the meat through the mincer and finish with a nice Roscoff onion.

2 options: 1 – mix everything together, put it in a gratin dish and bake in a hot oven (20 min at 220°) (photos); 2 – line the dish with half the mashed potato, then add the meat and finish with the rest of the mash.

notes: As a variation: Jerusalem artichoke parmentier, with 150 g potatoes and 150 g Jerusalem artichokes.

parties.nom: The day before: cooking the oxtail
etapes: Put the meat in cold water in a pressure cooker and bring to the boil.
Add the salt, pepper, garlic and all the vegetables, peeled, washed and cut into large pieces, then the bouquet garni.
Close the pressure cooker and cook on the “meat” setting for 35' from when the valve starts to hiss.

parties.nom: On the day: cooking the sauce charcutière
ingredients: 300 ml of the pot-au-feu broth above
etapes: Put the butter and the finely chopped onions in the sauce maker, fry for a few minutes on setting 3, add the flour and stir for 3'.
Pour in the white wine and the broth, season with salt and pepper. Cook for 30' on setting 3, then 5.
Go back to setting 2 to add the mustard and gherkins. Let it stir on 2 for a few minutes until ready to serve.

notes: Note: the unused vegetables and pot-au-feu broth will make the evening soup.

etapes: Remove the mushroom stalks and cook the caps in a little melted butter, season with salt and pepper.

Pan-fry the tournedos: sear them well, then cook over low heat, keep warm. Deglaze the pan with the port and add the cream, stirring until it just comes to the boil. Top the tournedos with the mushroom caps, coat with the sauce and garnish with chopped parsley.
Serve with matchstick potatoes or pommes dauphines.

notes: Wine: red Bordeaux, Saint-Émilion or Côtes du Rhône Châteauneuf-du-Pape.

etapes: Dress the duck. Place it in a roasting dish with oil, salt and pepper. Put it in a hot oven for about 1h20. Baste it frequently during cooking.

Make a sauce base by frying the duck giblets, the chopped onion and the cut carrots in butter. Add veal stock, the tomato purée, the white wine, the water and the bouquet garni. Season with salt and pepper, then cook uncovered over very low heat for 1 hour. Strain through a chinois.

In a saucepan, make a gastrique with the sugar and vinegar. When the gastrique is golden, add the duck stock made earlier, the zest strips of 3 oranges, blanched beforehand, along with their juice and the Grand Marnier.
When the duck is cooked, place it on a serving dish decorated beforehand with orange segments, and cover it with some of the zest strips.
Carve and serve with the orange segments and the zest strips, drizzled with the sauce.
Peel the fennel bulb and steam it. Set aside.
Separately, let a bag of couscous for 2 swell for 10 min in a saucepan of boiling salted water to which the zest of the (unwaxed) oranges has been added. Set aside.
Peel the onion and cut it into thin rings. Fry it in olive oil in a frying pan until nicely golden. Set aside.
Score the skin of the duck breasts in a criss-cross pattern and cook them skin side first, 3 min per side, in a casserole dish to avoid fat splattering.

Take out the duck breasts and wrap them in 2 layers of foil. Remove the excess fat, add the fennel, onion, couscous and orange juice, stir and let simmer until the orange juice has reduced almost completely.
Add the duck breasts and simmer a few more minutes. Slice the meat and serve.

notes: The photo shows a version with less reduced orange juice.

etapes: Heat a little oil in a casserole dish, then brown the duck legs on both sides until golden. Take them out of the pot, pour off most of the oil, put them back and continue cooking for another 30 min.

Halve the pears, carefully remove the core, and brown them on all sides in a frying pan with a little salted butter. When they are golden, add them to the casserole dish 5 min before the end of cooking.
Serve immediately.

ingredients: 2 pears (or 2 peaches) browned in salted butter as above
etapes: Preheat the oven to 250° and cook the duck breast skin side down for 15 min, then turn it onto the meat side for 10 min at 180°.
Remove the excess fat, add the browned pears and their cooking juices, and put back in the oven, switched off but still hot, for 5 min, the time it takes to eat the starter.

notes: The peaches are prepared exactly like the pears.

ingredients: 1 glass of water or, better, chicken stock
etapes: In a casserole dish, brown the duckling in 1 tbsp olive oil, whole or cut up depending on the size of the pot, after seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Add the sliced onions and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the glass of white wine, the stock, the honey and the raisins, soaked beforehand in a bowl of water and drained.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour.
15 minutes before the end of cooking, add the drained chestnuts.
Serve on warm plates.
Wash and stone the mirabelles. Peel and wash the potatoes. Season the legs with salt and pepper.
Heat a little duck fat in a casserole dish and brown the meat. Add the onion cut into 6, let it soften and turn golden.
Cook for 40 min; at the end of cooking, add the mirabelles and leave on the heat for another 10 min.
While the meat is cooking, boil the potatoes, cut into 4, “à l'anglaise”.

notes: The potatoes tone down the sweetness of the mirabelles a little.

filet-de-canette-aux-endives-et-raisins-.titre: Duckling breast with endives and raisins

ingredients: Endives steamed for 20' in a pressure cooker
½ glass of dry white wine
60 g currants soaked in a little water for about ½ h
etapes: In an ovenproof dish, place the duckling breast skin side down.
Around it, arrange the sliced onion and the drained currants.
Season the breast with salt and pepper, drizzle it with olive oil, then a thin layer of honey.
Pour the white wine around the breast.
Put in the oven, preheated to 220° fan, on shelf 1, for 15', then turn the breast over and move the dish to shelf 2 for another 15'.
5' before the end, add the endives around the breast.

gesiers-de-canard-confits-salade-frisee-.titre: Duck gizzard confit, frisée salad and pommes dauphines

etapes: Fry the gizzard confit in a frying pan with a little duck fat.
In another frying pan, brown the pommes dauphines in a little duck fat.
Serve on warm plates with frisée salad.
Put the potatoes in a saucepan of cold salted water and cook for about 20 minutes.
Peel them and cut them into dice.
In a large frying pan, melt the duck fat and fry the potatoes, the onion cut into strips and the finely chopped garlic clove.
When the potatoes start to turn lightly golden, add the gizzard confit.
Keep frying for about 10 min, until nicely golden. Season with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Serve hot.

ingredients: One small liqueur glass of Cointreau or Grand Marnier
etapes: Cook the duck breast for 30' in the oven on shelf 2 at 220° (after lightly oiling it with olive oil, seasoning with salt and pepper, and placing it skin side down, scored, in the lightly greased dish), for 15 min, then turn it over and leave for another 10 min, but at 180°.
Meanwhile, blanch the zest in a little water, set aside.

Bring the juice of the orange to the boil, stir in the zest (and its water), the Maïzena mixed beforehand with a little cold water, and 1 tsp sugar to make a sauce; keep warm. Before slicing the cooked duck breast thinly, don't forget to stir in the liqueur.
Serve on warm plates, with pommes dauphines on the side, for example.
Score the duckling breast in a criss-cross pattern and brush with a tbsp of honey. Sprinkle with thyme and season to taste.
Brown skin side down for 3 min in a buttered frying pan. Once the meat is seared, put it in the oven for 10 min.
Reheat the pan and deglaze with the red wine. Let it reduce, then add the jam, with the fresh redcurrants on top.
Slice the meat, then serve coated with sauce. Finish by adding a few fresh redcurrants on top.

notes: In the photo, served with fennel-couscous.

etapes: Before cooking the duck breasts, remove the excess fat and lightly score the skin in a criss-cross pattern. In a casserole dish (to minimise splattering), sear the breasts skin side first. Let them colour nicely, turn them over, season with salt and pepper, and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 min so they stay pink.
Meanwhile: squeeze 3 mandarins, take the zest of two others (if untreated before harvest), and reduce in a frying pan.
Once the duck breasts are cooked, set them aside (in the oven at 50° with the plates that are warming up).

In the duck's cooking juices (remove the excess fat), add the rest of the mandarins, peeled and in segments, fry them for 3 minutes, then add the sauce, which should be thickened with Maïzena if it is too runny.
Slice the duck breasts and arrange the plates with the sliced meat and the mandarin segments as in the photo, then coat with the sauce.

Cook the duck breast for 30' in the oven on shelf 2, fan at 220°, after lightly oiling it with olive oil, seasoning with salt and pepper, and placing it skin side down in the lightly greased dish, then turning it halfway through.
Meanwhile, cook the turnips, peeled and cut into small cubes, covered, in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat with enough butter for about twenty minutes, keeping an eye on them.
At the end of cooking, turn up the heat, season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with 2 to 4 tbsp caster sugar (to taste) and let them brown.
Serve on warm plates.
Cut up the spring chicken and brown it in the butter and oil. When the pieces are golden, pour off the excess fat.
Sprinkle with flour and let it colour for a few moments.
Pour in the calvados and the red wine, add the shallots, garlic, carrot, bouquet garni and tomato purée, season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for about 30'.
Separately, fry the lardons, the onions and the sliced button mushrooms.
Remove the pieces of chicken with a slotted spoon, place them on the serving dish surrounded by the garnish (onions, bacon, mushrooms) and pour the cooking sauce over everything.
Serve on warm plates.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C (gas mark 6) on fan setting. Lightly grease a gratin dish with olive oil. Place the turkey leg in the dish.

Peel the garlic cloves and the onion. Make incisions in the turkey flesh and insert the cloves into the leg. Arrange the sliced onion all around. Roughly break the bay leaf into the dish. Season generously with salt and pepper. Put in the oven for a quarter of an hour.
Deglaze with the white wine. Return to the oven for another quarter of an hour. Then baste with 20 cl chicken stock and cook for another quarter of an hour.
Turn the turkey leg over. Baste with the remaining stock. Scatter the chestnuts all around and return to the oven for 45 min. Keep an eye on it and baste regularly until it is cooked. Serve hot.

ingredients: 1 nice turkey fillet per person, about 150 g
1 glass of good dry white wine
etapes: Brown the turkey fillets in a frying pan over high heat in the butter and oil.
Add the sliced onion and fry until the onion is just right.
Add the flour and mix well, season with salt and pepper, add the glass of white wine and stir.
Cover, lower to medium heat and cook for about 20'.
Wash, stone and halve the apricots; move the fillets aside to free up as much of the sauce as possible and lay the apricot halves in it, rounded side up.
Continue cooking over medium heat, covered, for 5 to 10'.
Serve with plain boiled rice.

dinde-aux-marrons.intro: Pressure-cooker recipe: 45 minutes instead of 1h30 in the oven. On the other hand, the meat is much less tasty!

ingredients: 1 jar of 420 g vacuum-packed peeled chestnuts
etapes: Make a few slits in the flesh with a knife and insert slivers of garlic.

Rub the leg well with oil by hand, place it in the pressure cooker and season with coarse salt. Add the bay leaves and a few turns of the pepper mill. Add the sliced onion, brown both sides of the leg over high heat, then pour in the white wine.
Cook for 35 min, valve on position 2.
Open the pressure cooker, add the chestnuts and simmer for 10 min over low heat, uncovered.
Oil an ovenproof dish, place the oiled leg in it skin side down and season with coarse salt. Add the bay leaves and a few turns of the pepper mill. Add the sliced onion.
Put in the oven at 200° for 30 min.

Turn the leg over (*), add a little water if necessary and cook for another 30 min. Then add the chestnuts around the leg for 10 min. Baste with the cooking juices and add a little more water if necessary.

notes: (*) You can also plan to serve potatoes with the turkey. In that case, add the potatoes, peeled and cut into 4, at this point.

etapes: In a casserole dish, brown the rabbit pieces in a little oil and a good knob of butter; when they start to colour, add the sliced onion and continue browning everything.
Meanwhile, mix the mustard, crème fraîche, salt and pepper, pour the mixture over the rabbit and stir to spread it well over the meat.
Add the white wine and the sliced carrots.
Close the pressure cooker and cook at pressure 2 for 20 minutes.

notes: PS: the mushrooms in the photo were just “for looks”, the flavours don't go together.

etapes: Peel the celery, shallots and garlic. Cut them into small dice.

Heat the oil and butter in the casserole dish. Gently brown the rabbit pieces. When they are golden, add the vegetables. Fry them for 5 min, then pour over the calvados and flambé. Pour in the cider. Bring to the boil. Season with salt and pepper, add the bouquet garni. Cover and cook over low heat for 45 min.
At the end of cooking, add the crème fraîche. Mix well. Let it reduce for a few minutes so that the sauce thickens nicely. Adjust the seasoning. Sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve.

notes: Serve with baked apples, or boiled potatoes.
To drink: red Sancerre or dry cider.

rable-de-lapin-aux-pruneaux-et-carottes.titre: Saddle of rabbit with prunes and carrots

ingredients: 1 glass of white wine or cider
etapes: Stuff the saddle with some of the prunes, then brown it in the pressure cooker with the oil and the sliced onion.
When everything is nicely golden, season with salt and pepper.

Pour in the white wine (or cider). Add the apple, peeled and cut into pieces, the rest of the prunes, the garlic, and the veal stock dissolved in 1 glass of water (30 seconds in the microwave) plus ½ glass of water.
Close the pressure cooker on “2” and steam for 30 to 35 minutes.
Add the crème fraîche and simmer, stirring, for a few min.
Serve with steamed carrots.

pintade-aux-abricots-et-potimarron.titre: Guinea fowl with apricots and red kuri squash

ingredients: 1 Label Rouge free-range guinea fowl, cut into pieces
1 chicken stock cube dissolved in 2 glasses of hot water
etapes: Rehydrate the dried apricots in a bowl of lukewarm water.
In the pressure cooker, brown all the guinea fowl pieces, seasoned with salt and pepper, in the olive oil until nicely golden.
Take them out of the pot and fry the sliced onions for a few minutes.
Put the guinea fowl back on top of the onions and sprinkle with a little cinnamon.
Add the drained apricots and the juice of the half lemon, then the chicken stock.
Cook at pressure 2 for 15'.
Serve with a red kuri squash purée.

pintade-aux-marrons-et-raisins-ou-aux-po.titre: Guinea fowl with chestnuts and raisins, or with apples

ingredients: 1 glass of water or, better, chicken stock
etapes: In a casserole dish, brown the guinea fowl in 1 tbsp olive oil, whole or cut up depending on the size of the pot, after seasoning it with salt and pepper.
Add the sliced onions and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the glass of white wine, the stock, the honey and the raisins, soaked beforehand in a bowl of water and drained.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour.
15 minutes before the end of cooking, add the drained chestnuts.
Serve on warm plates.

notes: As a variation: instead of the chestnuts, serve with apples sautéed in butter with a little acacia honey.

ingredients: Andouillettes de Troyes “Nos régions ont du talent” (Leclerc)
etapes: Steam the potatoes in their skins. Peel them and cut them into cubes. Keep warm.
In a frying pan, fry the shallots cut into strips in a tablespoon of olive oil; keep them warm as soon as they are nicely golden.
Cook the andouillettes, cut into thick slices, on both sides, keep warm.

Make the Munster cream: in a heavy-bottomed saucepan, gently heat 150 g crème fraîche, gradually add 150 g Munster cut into small pieces, stirring constantly with a small whisk, add a little Gewurztraminer and stir in the shallots.
Heat the oven to 180°.
Put the andouillettes and potatoes in a buttered gratin dish, pour over the Munster cream and put in the oven for 5 min.
Brown on all sides for 20 min (cooked through) in a frying pan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, prepare mashed potatoes, sautéed potatoes or chips.
Serve with salad.

notes: My preference: genuine andouillettes de Troyes, “Nos régions ont du talent”, Leclerc brand.

ingredients: Andouillettes de Troyes « Nos régions ont du talent » (Leclerc)
etapes: Peel the potatoes and boil them for 20 min in salted water.

Remove the "skin" from the andouillettes, cut them in 4 lengthwise and into slices crosswise, then the slices into 1 cm strips and, once the strips are gathered together, cut them into 1 cm pieces. Mix.
Cut the onion into small pieces and soften them in the pan in the pork fat. Add the cut andouillettes and the white wine, and leave to simmer and reduce.
Pour into a gratin dish, cover with the mashed potato and bake (gas mark 6) for 20 minutes.

boudin-aux-chataignes-deux-purees-et-pom.titre: Chestnut black pudding, two purées and caramelised apples

ingredients: Two portions of black pudding with chestnuts
etapes: Make a red kuri squash purée.
Make a mashed potato purée.
Peel the 2 apples and cut them into small wedges. Brown them in the butter over medium heat, then caramelise them with the sugar over high heat.
Meanwhile, heat the black puddings over medium heat.
Serve the black puddings with the apples, surrounded by the two purées, on warm plates.

notes: As a variation: sweet potato or chestnut purée, white pudding/black pudding.

etapes: Soak the prunes, apricots and raisins in a bowl of hot water for 2 hours to plump them up.
When ready to cook, peel the apple and cut it into slices.
Melt 10 g butter in a casserole dish, add the apple slices, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Drain the dried fruit and add it to the apples. Season with salt and pepper, mix gently and cook for another 2 minutes, covered.
Set the fruit aside in the uncovered casserole dish.
Prick the black puddings with a fork so the skin doesn't burst during cooking.
Brown them on all sides. Cover the dish and cook for 1 min 30 on each side. Season with salt and pepper halfway through cooking.
Serve with the fruit on warm plates.
When ready to cook, peel the apple and cut it into slices.

Melt 10 g butter in a casserole dish, add the apple slices and cook over high heat, turning them often, until nicely golden. Season with salt and pepper; cover and leave for 10 minutes over low heat. Set aside.
Prick the black puddings with a fork so the skin doesn't burst during cooking.
Brown them on all sides. Cover the dish and cook for 1 min 30 on each side. Season with salt and pepper halfway through cooking.
Serve with the apples on warm plates.

ingredients: 700 g pork (prime rib chops or shoulder): have the bone ends trimmed and the chops partly cut

etapes: Peel the carrots and onion and cut them into small dice, and make a sauce base by frying them in butter. Add the juice of 6 clementines, season with salt and pepper, mix well, bring to the boil, add the veal stock, leave to reduce by half, then cook over very low heat for 1 hour.

Peel 8 clementines, squeeze 3 others and add the honey. In an ovenproof dish, arrange the 8 clementines and put them under the grill on setting 1 or 2, basting them often with the juice (a strong grill would make them burst). Repeat as many times as necessary until they are glossy.
Once both preparations are done, leave to cool and refrigerate until the next day.
Put the rack of pork, oiled with olive oil, into the oven set to grill position 3. Brown it well on all sides.
Switch the oven to 180° combined heat for 1 hr 15, and continue cooking, basting often with the rest of the previous day's honeyed clementine juice.
Present the plates, each with the whole clementine, 1 clementine in segments and the sauce.
Once it is cooked to your liking, take the roast out of the oven and cut the 4 chops.

Move the roasting dish up 2 notches and add a rack below it for the pre-garnished plates (1 whole clementine and one in segments per person). Put the chops back in the dish to brown the pale sides for 5 min, while the plates warm up.
Turn off the oven and finish the plates. Serve, it's delicious!

notes: In the photo, you can see that slices of steamed carrot were added as an extra.

ingredients: 300 g white beans from the garden
etapes: Steam the white beans for 10'.
Skin the tomatoes, salt them generously and leave them to lose some of their water in a colander.
Then cook the tomatoes with a big knob of butter and a large garlic clove until you have a nice thick tomato sauce.
Cook the sausages separately with a little butter.
Put the cooked sausages with the beans and the tomato sauce and leave to simmer for a while so the sausages flavour everything.

cotes-de-porc-aux-choux-de-bruxelles-et-.titre: Pork chops with Brussels sprouts and chestnuts

etapes: After peeling and washing the Brussels sprouts, throw them into a large quantity of boiling salted water and cook for 15 min over medium heat. Drain them.

In a casserole dish, melt the butter, add the sprouts and let them fry for a few moments. Add the chestnuts, season with salt and pepper and cook for 10 min uncovered, stirring very gently from time to time.
When ready to serve, pour the sprouts into the serving dish, lay the pan-fried pork chops on top and pour over the meat's cooking juices.

endives-au-jambon-bechamel-aux-3-farines.titre: Chicory and ham gratin, three-flour béchamel

ingredients: 2 or 4 chicory heads depending on size (variations: a nice fennel bulb or leeks)
etapes: Steam the chicory in the pressure cooker for 20 minutes and drain as thoroughly as possible. If using fennel, cook it in boiling salted water for about fifteen minutes.
Roll the ham slices around the chicory or the thinly sliced fennel.
In an ovenproof dish, spread some of the sauce over the bottom, arrange the ham rolls and cover with the rest of the béchamel.
Brown in the oven on fan heat at 220°, on the 2nd shelf, for about 20', keeping an eye on it, and serve when the top starts to turn golden.

Make the béchamel sauce in a saucier pan by cooking the flours in the butter on 3, add the milk, season with salt and pepper and cook for 20' on 5; at the end of cooking, add a pinch of ground nutmeg then the Gruyère, and keep warm on 2.

Cook the tenderloin in the pressure cooker: after softening the onion until golden in a big knob of butter and a drizzle of oil, add the tenderloin studded with the garlic clove and brown it on all sides, season with salt and pepper and add the white wine. Close the cooker and cook for 20 min.
Check that it is cooked, remove the tenderloin, slice it and set aside on plates kept warm in the oven.
Over low heat, add the crème fraîche and the Maroilles cut into small cubes to the cooking sauce. The Maroilles will melt gradually. The sauce is ready once it is nice and creamy.
Cover each plate of hot meat with the sauce.
Serve quickly with tagliatelle.
Wash and stone the mirabelles. Season the pork with salt and pepper.
With a large knife: cut the tenderloins in two, pierce them lengthwise and stuff them with mirabelles so that a mirabelle centre shows when sliced.

Heat the butter in a pressure cooker and brown the meat in it. Then pour in two cups of water (dissolve the 1/2 chicken stock cube in one of them), half the mirabelles cut into pieces, the cognac, the sugar, the pinch of ground cinnamon and the lemon juice.
Cook for 20 min. At the end of cooking, thicken the sauce with the cornflour.
With the rest of the mirabelles sautéed in butter in a frying pan, slice the tenderloin into rounds and present it on the plates with the sauce, the sautéed mirabelles and fresh pasta.
Stuff the tenderloin with as many prunes as possible.
Brown it in the casserole with the oil and the sliced onion.

When everything is nicely golden, season with salt and pepper and add a pinch of ground ginger, moisten with the white wine, add the apple peeled and cut into quarters, the rest of the prunes, the garlic, and the veal stock dissolved in 1 glass of water (30 seconds in the microwave) plus ½ glass of water.
Close the pressure cooker on "2" and steam for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve with potatoes boiled in salted water and cut into quarters, or with steamed carrots.

notes: Photos: with carrots; with potatoes.

ingredients: 1 pork steak per person, or Toulouse sausage
etapes: Prepare the cabbage and cook it in two lots of water (the second salted).
Fry the sliced onion, set aside.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into pieces and boil them, set aside.
Cook the pork steaks or the sausages right through, set aside.
Fry the cabbage in butter and add the onions. Serve as soon as the meat is ready.
Desalt the knuckle for the time indicated on the packaging.

Blanch the knuckle for a few minutes, drain, then put it back in the pressure cooker, cover the meat with water, add the carrots cut into large pieces, the bouquet garni, the garlic, and 1 onion studded with 3 cloves, easy to remove at the end of cooking if possible.
Cook for 40' at pressure 2. At the end of cooking, drain the knuckle, take the meat off the bone, remove the rind and cut it into small pieces.
Meanwhile, cook the lentils in a large quantity of water for 20'.

In a non-stick frying pan, brown the remaining sliced onion with a little butter and the lardons, add the rind, fry, and add the white wine. Once the liquid has been absorbed, add the tbsp of flour, then slowly a ladle of the cooking broth. Thicken while stirring, adding more broth if needed.
Stir in the drained lentils, the carrots and the meat: lower the heat and leave to simmer for 20', keeping an eye on it.
Brown the meat in butter with a drizzle of oil, remove the meat and the juices.
Fry the lardons and the sliced onion. Add the tbsp of honey.
Put the meat and sauce back, add the beer, salt lightly and season with pepper.
Cover and leave to simmer over medium heat for two hours.

notes: Serve with boiled potatoes on warm plates.
Drink: red wine (Madiran).

joues-de-porc-a-la-creme-et-a-la-moutard.titre: Pork cheeks with cream and mustard

etapes: In the casserole, brown the pieces of cheek on all sides in 2 tbsp olive oil.
Add the sliced shallots and fry them gently over low heat.
Add the white wine, then the crumbled ½ beef stock cube.
Pressure-cook on 2 for 25'.
At the end of cooking, stir the mustard and crème fraîche into the juices and reduce for a few minutes over low heat.
Adjust the seasoning and add the chives.

notes: Serve with tagliatelle.

joues-de-porc-confites-au-cidre.intro: Two versions: no. 1 with carrots, no. 2 with potatoes.

etapes: Peel the carrots and cut them into small dice.
Peel the shallots and slice them.
Cut the pork cheeks into pieces. Marinate them with the cider, shallots, carrots and bouquet garni for 24 hours.
Peel the onions and slice them.
Drain the meat and vegetables and keep the marinade.
Season the pieces of meat with salt and pepper.
Brown them in a casserole dish with the olive oil.
Fry the onions and lardons with the rest of the oil in the casserole dish.
Add the tomato purée and a pinch of sugar and mix.
Add the meat and the marinade back in.
Season with salt and pepper and adjust the seasoning. Cook for 1 hour over low heat.
When ready to serve, sprinkle with chopped parsley. Serve with homemade mashed potato.
Brown the pork cheeks for about 10 minutes in a mixture of oil + butter, then set aside.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into wedges. Dry them to remove excess starch.
Peel and cut the onion (into fairly large pieces). Bone the pork belly (keep the rind) and cut it into thick lardons.
Fry the pork belly and onions over high heat in a mixture of oil + butter, then add the potatoes and let them fry for about 10 minutes.
Then add the reserved pork cheeks. Season to taste (salt, pepper, herbes de Provence). Pour the cider over everything.
Lower the heat and leave to simmer for 1 hr 30, covered, skimming from time to time.
Remove the lid and continue cooking for at least 30 minutes.
The sauce should coat the potatoes. If the sauce is not reduced enough and you are short of time, take it out, transfer it to a saucepan and reduce it, then pour it over the meat.

notes: Serve hot with a green salad.

etapes: In the pressure cooker, fry the onion in olive oil, then add the pork cheeks without letting them brown.
Add the carrots, the potatoes cut into rounds, the leek cut into chunks and the sliced mushrooms. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the cloves, the bay leaves and the whole garlic. Moisten with the white wine and 1 glass of water. Cook for 1/2 hr.

notes: Note: we were out of carrots! So they're not in the photo. It's good anyway, but better with them!

palette-de-porc-aux-lentilles-vertes-du-.titre: Pork shoulder with green Puy lentils

etapes: Rinse the shoulder, put it in the pressure cooker, cover it with water, season with pepper, add 1 carrot, 1 onion studded with a clove, 2 garlic cloves, 1 bouquet garni and 1 glass of white wine. Close the cooker on 2 and cook for 55' once the steam starts.
Meanwhile, cook the lentils in 3 times their volume of water with the carrot, the onion, the remaining garlic cloves, pepper, the bouquet garni and 1 glass of white wine for 20'.
Reheat everything with a little meat juice when ready to serve.

ingredients: Shoulder roast (tastier, less dry and cheaper!) 500 to 600 g
etapes: In the pressure cooker, brown the roast in the oil on all sides until nicely golden, then add the onion cut into 8.
Add the apples, peeled and cut into 8, then the white wine (½ glass is enough).
Close the cooker and start cooking for 45 min.
Peel the potatoes, wash them and cut them in 4 lengthwise; add them 15 min before the roast has finished cooking.
Serve the roast sliced with the potatoes, and pour over the sauce from the roast (with the crushed apples and onion).

notes: As a variation, the potatoes can be replaced with apples.

rouelle-de-porc-aux-oignons-et-pommes-de.titre: Pork leg steak with onions and potatoes

etapes: Take the meat out of the fridge at least 1 hour beforehand.
In a very hot pressure cooker, pour in the olive oil, dot it with knobs of butter and lay in the pork, with the surrounding fat removed. Brown it on both sides and season with salt and pepper.
Place the onions, peeled and halved, on top and add a glass of white wine. Close the cooker, valve on position 2 (meat), and cook for 30' from when the steam starts.
Meanwhile, peel the potatoes, wash them, make a slit in each and slip in a bay leaf.
After 30 min, open the cooker (once the steam has gone), let the cooked onions fall into the sauce, add the potatoes and cook again for 12 min on position 1.

saucisse-de-morteau-aux-lentilles-et-car.titre: Morteau sausage with lentils and carrots

etapes: Cook the lentils in 3 times their volume of water (10 min in the pressure cooker with the carrots, peeled and cut into rounds).
Reheat the Morteau sausage for 20 min in simmering water.
Serve the drained lentils, add the crème fraîche and the sausage.

notes: Bon appétit.

ingredients: ¼ to ½ cabbage depending on size
etapes: Remove any damaged leaves from the cabbage and cut it into 4.

In the pressure cooker, cook the cabbage in two different lots of water: blanch for 5 min in boiling water, then refresh in cold water. Bring a second lot of water to the boil in the cooker. Cook for 5 min from when the valve starts turning (on 1).
Slice the onion, sweat it and brown it, set aside.
Cook the sausages thoroughly on all sides with a big knob of butter, set aside but keep the cooking juices.
