Put the onions back in the frying pan along with the cabbage, mix, brown the cabbage well, adding a little butter if necessary, put the sausages on top and leave to simmer for 5 min, especially if the cabbage has released some water.
Serve.

saucisses-aux-bettes-et-tomates.titre: Sausages with Swiss chard and tomatoes

etapes: Peel the garden tomatoes and cook them with a garlic clove. Season with salt and pepper, set aside.
Prepare the chard (cut into 3 cm pieces, removing the strings), throw it into boiling water and cook for 10 min in the pressure cooker. Set aside.
Cook the sausages for 20 to 25 min, turning them regularly so they brown well.
At the end of cooking, add the chard and the tomatoes and simmer over low heat for 10 min. Serve.
Peel the onion, cut it into thin slices and brown it. Set aside.
Peel the garden tomatoes and cook them with a garlic clove. Season with salt and pepper, set aside.
Peel, cut in half lengthwise, remove the central part containing the seeds, cut into thick rounds and cook for 10 min in the pressure cooker. Set aside.
Cook the sausages for 20 to 25 min, turning them regularly so they brown well.
At the end of cooking, add the courgettes, onions and tomatoes and simmer over low heat for 10 min.

saucisses-de-montbeliard-a-la-puree-de-p.titre: Montbéliard sausages with split pea purée

etapes: Wash the split peas in cold water.
In the pressure cooker, cover them with three times their volume of water and cook for 12 min from when the valve starts turning.
Make the purée and add a big knob of butter.
Reheat the sausages for 15' in boiling water.

notes: To cook without a pressure cooker: bring the cold water to the boil, skim, cook for 30'. Make the purée, add a big knob of butter.

saucisses-de-morteau-salade-de-lentilles.titre: Morteau sausages, lentil salad with Morbier

ingredients: 180 g Morbier AOC cut into strips
etapes: Dress the lentils after cooking and use them warm.
Arrange the sausage slices and the Morbier on the lentils.
Garnish with slivers of red onion and sprinkle with chives.

saucisses-poelees-puree-de-potimarron-et.titre: Pan-fried sausages, red kuri squash and sweet potato purée

etapes: Fry the onion in a frying pan with a little butter.
Wash and scrub the squash, remove the seeds, then cut it into pieces without peeling it.
Peel the sweet potato, then cut it into pieces.
Steam for 25 minutes.
Mash the squash and sweet potato flesh, add the golden onions, the cream and the pinch of nutmeg, and salt.
Serve with the sausages.

notes: Bon appétit.

etapes: Brown the ribs in oil on all sides, set aside.
Fry the onions, peeled and sliced, set aside.
Peel all the potatoes and apples, cutting the potatoes into 4 and the apples into 8.
Put everything in the pressure cooker, not forgetting the chopped garlic and parsley, and add 2 glasses of white wine and ½ glass of water.
Cook for 30 min from when the valve starts turning, on position 2.
Slice the mozzarella. Flatten the chicken breasts and fill them with mozzarella and sage (keep a few leaves for decoration). Roll them up and hold them closed with wooden cocktail sticks.
Heat the oil in a casserole dish and brown the chicken breasts on all sides. Season with salt and pepper, add the chicken stock, then leave to simmer for about 10 min.

Meanwhile, make the sauce: heat the butter in a saucepan and sweat the peeled, sliced shallot. Add the vin jaune and reduce by three quarters, then strain through a sieve, pressing the shallots well to keep all the flavour.
Put the cooking liquid back in the saucepan and bring to a simmer. Pour in the cream, season with salt and pepper and reduce for a few moments.
Divide the chicken breasts among the plates, coat with the sauce, decorate with the reserved sage leaves and serve immediately.

notes: Calories: medium.

blancs-de-poulet-sauce-miel-et-balsamiqu.titre: Chicken breasts with honey and balsamic sauce

etapes: Brown the already cooked breasts, cut into small cubes, in a non-stick frying pan.
In a small saucepan, pour in the crème fraîche, honey and vinegar.

notes: Serve with basmati rice, bulgur or fresh pasta.
Note: OK, I put the rice on too late and couldn't take a photo of the "complete" dish, but even eating the rice separately it's really good!

etapes: Put the butter in a sauté pan and fry the thinly sliced shallot until coloured.
Once the shallots are golden, add the cream-mustard mixture and the breasts cut into small cubes. Leave to simmer over low heat until the pieces of breast are heated through.

notes: Serve with pasta or rice and steamed carrots.

poulet-au-couscous.intro: Using leftovers: wings and meat from the chicken carcass.

ingredients: A small tin of prepared couscous vegetables
etapes: Put the leftover chicken in a saucepan with the contents of the tin of couscous vegetables and heat over low heat.
For the couscous: bring 1 glass of salted water to the boil. Off the heat, add a tablespoon of oil, sprinkle in the glass of couscous grains and mix immediately. Cover for 5 min.
Add a knob of butter. Fluff up with a fork. It's ready!
Cut the breasts into strips (raw breasts or not).
In a sauté pan, fry the chicken breasts in 10 g butter until nicely golden, set aside.
Next, toast the almonds until golden, set aside.
Replace with the sliced onion, softened until golden over low heat (at the end of cooking, add 1 tbsp of the chicken juices, if the chicken was roasted).
Add the breasts, pour in the cream and the mustard, season with salt and pepper. Mix and cook for another 5 min.
Cook the tagliatelle in a large quantity of boiling salted water for the cooking time indicated. Drain and add the rest of the butter.
Mashed potato and sweet potato.

notes: Serve the breasts on warm plates, topped with the almonds.

ingredients: 2 chicken breasts (from a rotisserie chicken for the recipe as made, but of course possible with breasts bought raw)
etapes: Peel the carrots and onion and cut them into small dice, and make a sauce base by frying them in butter. Add the juice of 6 clementines, season with salt and pepper, mix well, bring to the boil, add the veal stock, leave to reduce by half, then cook over very low heat for 1 hour.
Reheat the breasts for 5 min in the sauce (or pan-fry them beforehand) and serve with ½ mandarin in segments.

notes: It's even better with a duck breast!

poulet-aux-citrons.intro: Using up the breasts. A roast or rotisserie chicken is too much for two. The breasts can be done with almonds or with an orange sauce, and the wings and the rest of the meat from the carcass with lemons, which is what I suggest below.

etapes: The day before, marinate the pieces in the juice of ½ lemon and ½ lime, a crushed head of garlic, 2 tbsp olive oil, a glass of white wine and a teaspoon of ginger.
Cook in a hot oven with the marinade for 20 min, basting during cooking, and serve with rice.

ingredients: 1 Label Rouge yellow (corn-fed) chicken (drawn, of course!)
1 tin of extra-fine peas or, better, 1 kg of fresh peas
etapes: Put the well-oiled chicken in a suitable dish in a hot oven (180°) for 1 h 15 to 1 h 30 depending on its weight.
To be sure the chicken is properly cooked, check at 1 h 15 by pulling the legs away a little to see that it is done.
Extend the cooking time accordingly or, if it is done, add the tin of peas, switch off the oven and wait 5 min before serving.
If using fresh peas, cook them with a few lettuce leaves and keep them warm while the chicken finishes cooking.

notes: Plan a salad!
Of course, the peas can be replaced by chips, green beans, broccoli, fennel…

blanquette-de-veau.titre: Blanquette de veau (veal in white sauce)

ingredients: 600 g of veal, half breast, half shoulder, cut into large pieces
2 glasses of good-quality dry white wine
etapes: Put the pieces of meat in a heavy-based pressure cooker, add the carrots cut in 4, the onion, the bouquet garni, salt and pepper. Cover with cold water, put on the heat, bring to the boil, skim, then add the white wine and the mushrooms, stalks removed, washed and roughly chopped. Pressure-cook on setting 2 for about 30 min.
In the sauce maker, make a roux with the butter and flour on setting 2, add ½ l of the cooking stock and cook on setting 5 for 20 min.
In a bowl, mix the egg yolk with the cream and the lemon juice: pour into the sauce and heat without boiling on setting 2.
Serve on warm plates with Creole rice, covering everything with the sauce from the sauce maker.

notes: Tip: so as not to waste the egg white, cook it in the meat juices before serving.

etapes: In a frying pan, brown the escalopes in the butter and oil.
When they have turned a nice golden colour on both sides, take them out of the pan, set them aside and pour away the fat they were cooked in.
Over the heat, in the clean pan, pour in the Madeira, bring it to the boil and add half the cream. Let it bubble for a few moments, then pour in the rest of the cream.
Put the escalopes back into this sauce, season with salt and pepper and leave to simmer gently for 10 min.
Serve on warm plates with cooked carrots.

ingredients: 4 celery sticks and a quarter of a celeriac
etapes: Put 2 l of water in a pressure cooker, bring to the boil, plunge in the shank, skim if necessary, and season with salt and pepper.
Add all the vegetables and pressure-cook on setting 2 for 45 min.
Serve on warm plates with mustard and mayonnaise.

roti-ou-cote-de-veau-a-la-creme-et-aux-c.titre: Veal roast or veal chops with cream and carrots

ingredients: 1 milk-fed veal roast from the rump, about 500 g
Butter, Isio oil, thyme, rosemary, salt, pepper, a little Muscadet
1 heaped tbsp of thick crème fraîche
etapes: Tuck the sprigs of thyme and rosemary under the string of the roast.
In a heavy-based casserole, brown the roast on all sides over a high heat in a large knob of butter with a drizzle of oil.
When the whole roast is nicely browned, add the sliced onion and the carrots cut into fairly thick rounds.
Season with salt and pepper and pour a splash of Muscadet over the meat.
Cover and lower to a medium heat.
Cook for about 30 min, keeping an eye on it and turning the meat regularly.
When the meat is cooked and has a nice even colour, remove the excess fat and deglaze the casserole with a heaped spoonful of crème fraîche.
Serve straight away on warm plates.
Brown 4 nice chops, take them out when they are cooked, and in their juices proceed as above for the onion and the carrots.

rouelle-de-veau-aux-pruneaux-ou-aux-mira.titre: Veal shank slice with prunes or mirabelle plums

ingredients: 35 g of butter and ½ tbsp of Isio oil
250 g of prunes and 50 g of raisins
etapes: Soak the prunes and raisins in cold water for 15 min.
In the pressure cooker, melt the butter with a drizzle of oil. Brown the veal first, then the onions and the carrots cut into rounds.
Sprinkle everything with a teaspoon of flour, stir gently and moisten with the stock made with the veal stock and the white wine.
Bring to the boil, season with salt and pepper and add the bouquet garni. Cover and simmer for 20 min from the moment the valve starts to turn.
Open the pressure cooker. Add the drained prunes and raisins. Close it again and leave to simmer gently for another 10 min.
Use 850 g of fresh mirabelle plums, washed, stoned and halved, instead of the prunes and raisins.

ingredients: 3 fresh tomatoes or 3 tbsp of tomato purée
etapes: Brown the veal with 1 tbsp of oil and 1 knob of butter over a high heat, season with salt and pepper, and add the sliced onions and the carrots cut into sticks.
Cook for 5 minutes and pour in the white wine, then add water just to cover the meat. Cook for 25 minutes at a boil.
Add the tomatoes, peeled and halved, with the garlic, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the drained tinned chestnuts and simmer again for about ten minutes.
Serve with the white chard stalks, blanched and sautéed in a pan.

notes: The onions and carrots can be cooked with a little water, a knob of butter, a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of sugar so that they glaze once the liquid has evaporated.
Note: for the chestnuts, go for « Le Clos du Châtaignier » in 400 g tins (at U).
If possible, a few pearl onions will look wonderful!

ingredients: ½ calf's head with the tongue, rolled by the butcher, 900 g
1 hard-boiled egg cut into small pieces
etapes: Rinse the roll, put it in the pressure cooker, cover it with water, boil for a few minutes, skim, then drain the meat, removing anything that may still be stuck to it.

Put the meat back in the pressure cooker, cover with water, add ½ glass of vinegar, season with coarse salt, and add the 2 carrots cut into large pieces, the bouquet garni and the onion with the cloves (making sure they are easy to fish out), then pressure-cook on setting 2 for 40 minutes. Keep the pressure cooker closed until you serve.
Make a vinaigrette with 2 tbsp of vinegar, 4 tbsp of oil, salt, pepper, and the chopped shallot and parsley; add the egg last.
When serving on warm plates, remove the thick skin from the tongue, cut the meat into large pieces and serve the vinaigrette on the side.

notes: Serve with boiled potatoes.

ingredients: 300 g of white or brown button mushrooms
1 tbsp or a small tin of tomato purée
etapes: Buy the veal already cut into pieces. Brown the meat in the butter and oil in a heavy-based casserole for about 5 min.
Remove the meat and, in its place, brown the sliced shallots and the carrots cut into rounds.
Put the meat back, season with salt and pepper, and add the bouquet garni, the tomato purée, the tomatoes and the garlic. Pour over the white wine.
Cover, bring to the boil, then simmer over a medium heat for 1 h.
Add the mushrooms cut into pieces and cook for another 1 h.
Serve on warm plates.

ingredients: ½ litre of white or red wine
etapes: With the eel skinned and cut into 6 cm pieces, in a pressure cooker, fry the carrot cut into rounds, the chopped onions and the crushed garlic in the butter.
Add the pieces of eel and fry for a few minutes. Season with salt and pepper, pour over the cognac and flambé. Add the wine and the bouquet garni. Bring to the boil.
Close the pressure cooker and cook over a low heat for 10 min from the moment the valve starts to turn.
Meanwhile, cut off the sandy base of the mushroom stalks and wash them. Slice them and sauté them briskly in a little butter.

Two minutes before serving, add the mushrooms to the matelote sauce (if the juices seem too thin, add ½ tsp of cornflour mixed with a little of the juices, stir into the sauce and let it thicken for a moment).

notes: Serve hot on warm plates.

anguille-rotie-garniture-de-celeri-et-ca.titre: Roast eel with celery and carrots

etapes: Over a high heat, brown the eel, skinned and cut into 6 cm pieces, in a little butter and oil; set aside.
Fry the carrot cut into rounds, the celery cut into cubes and the chopped onions.
In an ovenproof dish, lay the pieces of eel and sprinkle with crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Pour over the wine.
Slice the onion into rings and cover the fish with them. Sprinkle the onions with breadcrumbs (if you have no breadcrumbs, a crushed rusk will do perfectly well).
Put in a hot oven (180°, gas mark 6) for 30 min.

notes: Serve hot on warm plates.

bar-au-beurre-blanc-nantais.titre: Sea bass with Nantes beurre blanc
bar-au-beurre-blanc-nantais.intro: Sea bass (or white fish) with rice. Nantes beurre blanc made in the Seb sauce maker.

ingredients: A glass of long-grain white rice
etapes: Cook the fish for 10 min in a court-bouillon. Drain and prepare the fillets.
Put the finely chopped shallots in the sauce maker and sweat them for 2 to 3 min.
Pour in the white wine and season with salt and pepper. Set to position 5. Reduce by 3/4, switch the appliance off and leave to cool.
Set to position 2. Work in the butter in small pieces. The sauce should become frothy and thickened. Allow about 15 min.
Cook the white rice.
On warm plates, coat the fillets with the sauce, drain the white rice and serve.
Clean the vegetables; cut the carrots into rounds, the leek lengthways then into pieces, and the mushrooms into slices. Steam everything for 12 minutes.

Peel the shallots, slice them thinly and fry them in butter for 3 minutes; add the vegetables to the shallots with 1 glass of white wine and 3 spoonfuls of thinned crème fraîche, and season with salt and pepper.
Put the cod in a dish, cover it with the vegetables and the sauce, cover with foil and bake at 180° for 40 minutes. Position 3 of the left-hand knob on our oven.

ingredients: 300 g of cod, loin or fillets
etapes: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil with the bay leaf and a pinch of salt. Poach the fish in it for about 10 min.
Melt the butter in a saucepan with the mustard. Mix well and, once everything is smooth, add the cream while stirring.
Then add the lemon juice little by little. Season with salt.
Let it thicken for a few minutes over a low heat, stirring, then take off the heat.
When serving on warm plates, coat the fish with the sauce, sprinkle with snipped chives (or parsley), and serve with white rice.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the finely chopped shallot and the minced garlic. Fry everything for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with the white wine. Reduce the white wine by ¾.
Once reduced, transfer the mixture to a large bowl. Add the breadcrumbs, the parsley and the lemon juice, and season with salt and pepper.
Lay the fish fillets in an ovenproof dish, pour the olive oil over the fish, turn it over, spread the topping over the fish and bake for 15 min at 120°.

notes: Serve with white rice.

croustade-au-crabe.personnes: 4 or 6 people, depending on whether it is a starter or a main course

ingredients: 100 g of button mushrooms, preferably brown
For the béchamel: 50 g of butter, 50 g of flour, ½ l of milk, salt, pepper
etapes: Fry the mushrooms with the shallot, season with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Make the béchamel and cook it for 15 min in a sauce maker.
Scald the prawns if needed, depending on how they were stored.
Turn the oven on to conventional heat at 200°.
Roll the pastry out into a fairly deep tart dish and prick it all over.
Mix the crab, the mushrooms, the Gruyère and finally the prawns into the béchamel.
Pour the mixture into the dish and bake on the bottom shelf, first on conventional heat at 200° for 30 min, then for 15 min with the fan added.

notes: Serve with a salad.

ingredients: 500 g of tomato pulp (beefsteak tomatoes if possible)
1 glass of black Camargue rice or 1 glass of three-rice mix: brown, black, white
etapes: Peel the tomatoes (plunge them into boiling water for a few minutes), cut them into pieces and cook them for 10 min with some salt. Set aside.
In a casserole, pour in a little olive oil and add the chopped shallots; brown them and set aside.
Fry the peeled prawns, turning them, until they take on colour. Add the shallots and flambé with the cognac.

Add the tomato pulp with as little juice as possible, the fennel, the white wine and the chopped garlic. If needed, add a little water to cover the prawns (using the leftover tomato pulp juices, for example).
Season with salt and freshly ground pepper and a piece of dried orange peel. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes at a gentle simmer, covered.
Serve with the rice of your choice, cooked beforehand.
In a frying pan, pour a drizzle of olive oil, add the prawns, salt them and fry for 3 min on each side.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley and garlic. At the end of cooking, add the persillade to the prawns along with a squeeze of lemon. Stop the cooking.

Serve with short-grain rice: fry it in a little olive oil with ½ onion cut into small pieces, then add 2 glasses of water for 1 glass of rice and the grated carrot. Cook for 10 min over a low heat once it boils.

notes: Variation: pan-fried prawns with garlic and parsley.

etapes: Thaw the lobster tails for 13 min in boiling water, peel them, cut them into 1 cm rounds and brown them lightly for a few min in olive oil over a high heat. Set aside.
Lightly brown the chopped onions and shallots in the butter; set aside.

Cut the peeled tomatoes into small pieces in a frying pan and cook off their « water », then add the onions and shallots, the sliced garlic, the white wine and the cognac, season with salt and pepper, lay the lobster rounds on top and simmer for a good 5 minutes.

notes: Serve with white rice.

queues-de-langouste-et-endives-a-lorange.titre: Spiny lobster tails and chicory with orange

etapes: If the lobster tails are frozen, let them thaw at room temperature (30 min in cold water). Cut the tails in half lengthways.
Prepare the orange zest and blanch it in boiling water. Set aside.
Gently melt the butter in a sauté pan and add the oil. Brown the chicory, cut in 4, on all sides (10-15 min). Once cooked, set aside.
Replace them with the lobster, flesh side down. Cover and leave over a low heat for 15 min.
Remove the lobster, take it out of the shells, then put it back in. Arrange on warm plates and keep them in a hot oven.
Deglaze the pan with the orange juice, add the grated zest and the sugar, and boil for 1 to 2 min until the sauce is slightly syrupy.
Add the chicory and season with salt and pepper. Leave for 5 minutes over a low heat.
Take the plates out of the oven and add the garnish. Decorate with a sprig of dill.
Have the sea bream gutted and scaled (or use fillets). Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin rounds. Peel the onions. Peel the tomatoes and slice them thinly, along with the onions.
In a suitable ovenproof dish, lay a bed of potatoes, then a bed of tomatoes and the sea bream. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with thyme leaves and marjoram. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook at a medium heat for about 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 210°.
Scale, gut, rinse and drain the bream.

Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with olive oil to your liking, cover the bream with onion rings, and add the carrots cut into strips, ½ glass of white wine and ½ glass of water. Bake for 40 to 45 min.
Halfway through cooking, turn the bream over and add ½ glass of white wine.

notes: Use the time it takes to « carve » the fish to warm the plates in the hot oven.

dorade-sebaste-au-riz-ou-boulgour.intro: Recipe never written down: only the photo of the dish has been kept.

dorade-sebaste-carottes-a-la-creme-fraic.titre: Redfish with carrots in crème fraîche

etapes: Cook the carrots, peeled and cut into 1 cm rounds, in the pressure cooker; set aside.
Pan-fry the redfish fillets for 7 min on each side; set aside.
Peel and thinly slice the shallot, brown it in butter in the frying pan, add a splash of white wine and the crème fraîche, stir, finally add the carrots and simmer for 5 minutes over a low heat.

notes: Serve the redfish and the creamed carrots on warm plates.

filets-de-dorade-royale-sauce-a-l-orange.titre: Gilt-head bream fillets with orange sauce

ingredients: One nice gilt-head bream for two (800 g): have the fishmonger fillet it
For the court-bouillon: 1 leek, 1 carrot, 1 onion, salt, pepper, bay leaf, thyme, parsley
etapes: Remove the zest from one orange, then squeeze the oranges.
Salt the flesh of the fish.
In an ovenproof dish, lay the bream fillets flesh side down, skin side up, and cover with the court-bouillon, made in advance, up to the level of the skin, which should just touch the surface.
Bake at 200° or 210° (depending on the oven) for 20 min.

Meanwhile, bring the orange juice to the boil and whisk in the butter continuously, salt, bring to the boil again, then add the zest and the cornflour mixed beforehand with a little cold water, to obtain a smooth sauce.
Plate the fillets after removing the skin, and coat them with the sauce.

notes: Serve with rice.

ingredients: 50 g of home-grown tomato sauce per squid
etapes: Have the fishmonger clean the squid. Check the cleaning, especially at the bottom of the pouch. Cut into 1 cm rings.
Brown the squid in a large knob of salted butter for 5 min maximum, cover, turn off the heat and let it finish cooking like this for 20 min.
Meanwhile, make the tomato sauce with the finely chopped garlic, the parsley, salt, pepper and the white wine: adjust the quantities to the number of squid.
Finally pour the sauce over the squid and simmer for 1 to 2 min, uncovered.

notes: Serve on warm plates with white rice.

etapes: « Simply » fry the swordfish steak in butter in a frying pan like a tournedos, 3 to 4 min on each side.
Here the side dish is a bag of bulgur cooked in boiling water.
To decorate, add one or two tomato slices fried with the swordfish and a little parsley.
In an ovenproof dish, lay the fish on the oiled base and put the butter, cut into slivers, on top. Pour over the squeezed lemon juice. Decorate with slices of peeled lemon.
Then season with salt and pepper to taste. Bake for 10 min in the oven at 200°, then serve your halibut fillets on warm plates and enjoy straight away.

In a sauté pan, heat the olive oil with the crushed garlic. Fry the tomatoes, cut into pieces, for 4 to 5 min over a high heat, shaking the pan back and forth. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and keep warm.
Rinse the fish fillets and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 80 g of butter in a frying pan. Cook the fillets in it for 4 min on each side over a low heat. The butter must not burn and should stay golden. Remove the fillets and arrange them on a warm dish.

Add the lemon juice to the cooking butter. Off the heat, stir in the rest of the butter in small pieces. Pour this sauce over the fillets. Surround with the pan-fried cherry tomatoes and serve immediately.

notes: As a variation: the fillets can be sprinkled with paprika and served with capers, and the butter replaced with olive oil.
In the photo, the side dish is a mix of red long-grain and wild rice, but it can be replaced with boiled potatoes.

etapes: Cook the haddock in milk for 10 min and boil the potatoes in water for 15 min.
In a casserole, heat up the sauerkraut, then add the peeled potatoes and the haddock with its skin removed.

notes: Serve on warm plates with beer.

ingredients: A smoked haddock fillet of 300 to 400 g
etapes: Peel the potatoes and cut them in 4. Put them in a large saucepan, add a pinch of salt and the crushed garlic clove and cover with cold water. Put on a high heat with a lid.

Meanwhile, in a second saucepan, lay the haddock skin side up. Cover it with milk. Heat gently and, as soon as it starts to simmer, take the pan off the heat. Cover it and leave the haddock to « poach » in it for at least 10 min.

When the potatoes are cooked, drain them. Put them back in the pan. Mash them with a fork, add the crème fraîche and a little of the fish poaching milk (if it is too dry) and mix. Season with salt and pepper. Spread in an ovenproof dish.
Wash and finely chop the parsley. Drain the haddock and flake it into the dish, then sprinkle with grated Comté.
20 min before serving the meal, heat the oven to 180° for ¼ h. Bake the gratin for 5 min.
Before serving, sprinkle with the chopped parsley.

notes: Note: add ½ lemon per plate.

sushi-de-haddock-aux-lentilles-vertes-du.titre: Haddock « sushi » with Puy green lentils

ingredients: 1 smoked haddock fillet of about 200 g
1 glass of Puy green lentils = about 125 g
etapes: Put the lentils in 3 times their volume of cold water; bring to the boil and keep boiling over a moderate heat for 30 min: cook without salt; drain and set aside.

In the morning for lunch, cut the raw haddock fillet into thin slices, removing the skin (preferably use a haddock at least 10 days before its use-by date); leave it to marinate in the fridge in the lemon – olive oil – pepper mixture.
At mealtime, dress the cold lentils with most of the marinade (to taste), the sliced shallot, pepper and a tart apple cut into small cubes; arrange nicely on the plates; enjoy.

joues-de-lotte-a-la-creme-et-aux-epinard.titre: Monkfish cheeks with cream and spinach

etapes: Cook the spinach in a saucepan with butter, season with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Flour the monkfish cheeks and fry them in a frying pan with olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Cook them for about 10 min on each side until the bottom of the pan sticks a little.
Deglaze with enough white wine.
Add the parsley snipped with scissors and the garlic cut into small pieces, then add the crème fraîche and let it thicken.

notes: Serve with the reheated spinach on warm plates.
NB: use enough crème fraîche and white wine to get enough sauce for both the monkfish and the spinach.

etapes: Have the fishmonger fillet the monkfish.
Rinse the fillets in cold water and pat them dry.
Pan-fry the monkfish fillets with salted butter (medium heat, 6-7 min on each side). Set aside.
Cook the rice.
In a frying pan, put the (light) crème fraîche mixed with the mustard and the cooked monkfish fillets, and simmer for a few minutes.

notes: Serve on very hot plates.
Note: extra-fine green beans, boiled potatoes or plain couscous can just as well replace the rice.

etapes: Have the fishmonger fillet the monkfish.
Put the roughly crushed garlic between the 2 fillets, place them on baking paper in an ovenproof dish, season with salt and pepper and pour a drizzle of olive oil over everything.
Close the parcel and bake for 20 min in a fan oven at 200°.
Meanwhile, cook the rice for 13 min in salted water, drain and dress with the butter and the tomato sauce.
Open the parcel and serve everything on warm plates (reheat the rice in the microwave if needed).
Rinse the monkfish fillets (have the monkfish prepared when you buy it), pat dry and cut into 4 pieces. Dredge them in flour.
In a sauté pan, fry the pieces of fish in the oil. Once golden on both sides, take them out and set aside.

In the same sauté pan, lightly brown the finely chopped shallots, the peeled and crushed garlic clove and the tomatoes (skinned) cut in 4. Put the pieces of monkfish back, pour over the cognac and flambé.
Then add the tomato purée, the white wine, the salt, a pinch of pepper and the orange peel. Stir, cover and cook gently for 20 minutes.

notes: Serve on warm plates with white rice.

etapes: Rinse the fish in cold water and pat it dry.
In a sauté pan, brown the chopped onion and sliced garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Add the tomatoes (skinned), cut into quarters; season with salt and pepper.
Cook uncovered until it turns into a purée, then pass it through the food mill. Add a knife-tip of saffron.
Dip the fillets in the milk, then in the flour, and brown them in the rest of the oil, very hot.
Arrange the monkfish fillets in an oiled ovenproof dish; pour the sauce over them; sprinkle with grated cheese.
Put in a hot oven (180°) and cook for 20 minutes.

notes: Serve on warm plates, can be accompanied by white rice.

etapes: Rinse the monkfish fillets in cold water and dry them.
In a sauté pan, fry the chopped onions and sliced garlic in 2 tbsp of oil.
Add the tomatoes cut into quarters, season with salt and pepper and cook uncovered until it turns into a purée.
Pass the sauce through the food mill and add a pinch of saffron.
Dip the fillets in the milk, coat them in flour, then brown them in the rest of the oil, good and hot.
Arrange them in an oiled ovenproof dish, coat with the sauce and cover with grated cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes in a hot oven (gas mark 7).

notes: Recipe taken from a magazine clipping, retyped as a summary.

ingredients: A few sprigs of savory, thyme, rosemary
etapes: Peel and deseed the tomatoes. Cut the courgettes and peppers into large chunks, the aubergines into rounds (unpeeled), the tomatoes into quarters and the onions into slices.

Heat the oil in a casserole and fry the onions and peppers. When they are nicely browned, add the aubergines and courgettes. Fry them in turn (5 to 10 minutes), then add the tomatoes and 1 crushed garlic clove. Season with salt and pepper, and cook covered over a low heat for 15 min.
Cut a garlic clove into small pieces and stud the monkfish tail with them, as if it were a leg of lamb.

Transfer the vegetables to a large ovenproof dish. Lay the monkfish “leg” on top. Add the white wine and the sprigs of savory, thyme and rosemary. Cook in a hot oven (180°) for 35 to 40 min, basting often with the cooking juices.

Make a tomato sauce: fry the sliced red onion in enough butter in a non-stick frying pan, then add the sliced tomato and the finely chopped garlic clove, season well with salt and pepper and simmer for at least ½ hour over a low heat.

Cooking the monkfish, prepared by the fishmonger: rinse it, wipe it, coat it in flour and put it in a non-stick frying pan with enough melted butter over a medium heat; cook it for 15 min, turning it regularly and basting it with the melted butter; season with salt and pepper.
Rule to follow: do not cook it for more than 15 min, overcooked monkfish turns rubbery!
Serve and enjoy straight away, the monkfish topped with the tomato sauce, with a packet of couscous cooked for 1 min 30 at the very last minute.

ingredients: One small line-caught mackerel per person
etapes: Wash and gut the mackerel.
In a large casserole, prepare the court-bouillon, bring it to the boil, lower the heat so the water is just simmering, and put the mackerel in for about ten minutes.
Lift them out carefully and lay them in the serving dish; keep them warm.
The sauce: break 2 eggs, put the yolks in a bowl. Add a spoonful of mustard. Stir.
Heat a saucepan of water to warm the bowl in a bain-marie.
Add a dash of vinegar to the yolks, add the butter in small pieces to melt, stirring all the time; season with salt and pepper.
Pour this sauce over the mackerel and serve.

notes: When making this recipe, we preferred to present the fish without the sauce and put it directly on the plates, hence the photos.

etapes: Gut the mackerel, wash them and pat them dry. Lay them in an ovenproof dish.
Add the onion cut into rings, the chopped parsley, salt, pepper, the white wine, ½ glass of water, 3 slices of lemon (if available) and dot everything with knobs of butter.
Cook in a hot oven (200°), switched on beforehand (to avoid any risk of “burning”, put a sheet of aluminium foil on top for the first 10 minutes).
After 10 min, lower the temperature to 180° and cook for a good 10 more minutes.

notes: Side dish: boiled potatoes.

etapes: Gut and clean the mackerel, then lay them in an ovenproof dish.
Cover the fish with the gherkins, onion, lemon and carrot, cut into thin slices. Add the crumbled thyme, the bay leaves, salt and about ten peppercorns.
Pour the white wine over, cover with a sheet of aluminium foil and cook for 30 minutes in a moderate oven.
Leave to cool completely, then carefully transfer the mackerel to a terrine. Garnish them with the onion and carrot slices, pour the strained marinade over them and keep in a cool place.

notes: They keep for 2 to 3 days in the fridge.
During cooking, the fish should be bathed in the marinade: if necessary, add a little white wine diluted with water.
Choose small mackerel (known as “Dieppe” mackerel): the marinade penetrates the flesh better.
For a spicier version, add a small red chilli with the thyme and bay leaves.
To try.
Recipe taken from a magazine clipping, retyped as a summary.

etapes: Desalt the cod for 3 to 12 h (5 changes of water) according to the instructions on the packet (salting methods may differ).
Put it on to cook in cold water, letting it simmer for 10 min.
Cook the peeled potatoes in unsalted water and make them into a purée.
Flake the cod into a bowl and crush it with a pestle, work in the hot oil, finish crushing the cod, then work in the crème fraîche.
Mix well with the purée and add ¼ to ½ glass of milk to make the mixture creamier.
Put into a gratin dish in a hot oven for 20 min (220°).

notes: Serve with a salad dressed with an olive oil vinaigrette with garlic or shallot.

morue-a-la-parmentiere.titre: Salt cod with potatoes (à la parmentière)

ingredients: 750 g potatoes, boiled, peeled and cut into rounds
For the sauce: 50 g butter, 40 g flour, 1/4 l milk
etapes: Poach the cod starting from cold water, without letting it boil (it would toughen).
Drain it, flake it and arrange it in the serving dish, alternating with the potato slices. Keep warm.
Make a white roux with the butter and flour, add the crushed garlic, then the milk, and cook for a few minutes.
Add the grated Gruyère and cook for 5 more minutes.
Coat the cod with this sauce, sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

notes: Recipe taken from a magazine clipping, retyped as a summary.

etapes: Scrape and wash the mussels before cooking them over a high heat, covered, for a few minutes with the white wine.
Check that they have all opened: to do this, stir them from time to time. When they have all opened, take them off the heat and put them in a dish to cool.
Strain the juice through a chinois and reduce it by a third over a low heat.
Slice the shallots and brown them gently with a little butter in a small frying pan. Add the strained mussel juice, the cider, a little salt and the pepper, and reduce by a good third again.
In a bowl, mix the crème fraîche and the two egg yolks. Add them to the shallot, cider and wine mixture. Cook for two more minutes over a low heat, stirring.
Lay the mussels out flat on the plate. Coat them with the shallot sauce.
Cook for 5 to 10 min in a fan oven at 200°, serve at once.
Take 200 g of semi-preserved mussels, cooked plain; drain them, rinse them and arrange them in an earthenware dish.
Make the sauce as above, but without white wine, with only 1 egg yolk and 10 cl of crème fraîche.
Coat the mussels with this sauce, and bake in a fan oven at 200° for 8 min.

notes: Drink: white wine or Breton cider.
Side dish: tagliatelle or nids d’Alsace (nest-shaped egg pasta).

moules-marinieres-ou-au-riz.titre: Moules marinières or mussels with rice

ingredients: 1 large glass of dry white wine
etapes: Clean the mussels: brush them and pull off the beards if necessary. Rinse in cold water without leaving them to soak.
Chop the shallots and garlic and fry them in 50 g of butter in a large casserole.
Add the white wine, the snipped parsley and the bouquet garni, and simmer for 1 min.
Over a “high heat”, put the mussels in the casserole and cook for 4 to 6 min (depending on the size of the mussels), stirring from time to time with the skimmer.
Serve in soup plates with chips.
For mussels with rice, use the pilaf method.

ingredients: 1 tin of sliced button mushrooms (150 g)
etapes: Put the fish, cut into pieces, into the cold court-bouillon and cook for 10 min; drain and keep warm.
Melt the butter, add the flour and pour in ¼ litre of the court-bouillon. Cook for 10 min over a low heat, stirring (or use the sauce maker); do not add salt but do add pepper.
Add the egg yolk and the mushrooms to this sauce, then the fish, and heat through.

notes: Serve with steamed potatoes and golden croutons.
Note: if you can't get the right quantity of fish, take more, cook it all in the court-bouillon and freeze the extra for next time.

poisson-blanc-a-la-creme-et-aux-champign.titre: White fish with cream and mushrooms

etapes: Peel the onion and cut it into thin slices. Fry it in a small saucepan with olive oil for about 3 min.
Add the mushrooms and let them soften for 10 min.
Add the parsley and the crème fraîche, not forgetting the mustard; stir and cook covered for 12 min.
Put the plates in the oven at 80°.

Now it's time to see to the fish: wash them, coat them in flour, and cook the fillets in a frying pan with a little olive oil, 3 min on each side. Check they are done, and keep them warm while the mushrooms finish.
Place the fish on the warm plates and coat with the sauce and mushrooms.

notes: If needed, plan some boiled potatoes, piping hot and buttered.

ingredients: 1 skate wing per person or for 2 people depending on the weight of the fish
Black butter for 2 people: 50 g butter, 1 dash of vinegar, ½ small jar of capers
etapes: Wash the skate wings under running water, put them in a stockpot and cover them with water.
Heat to bring the water to a simmer, turn off the heat, cover, and leave to cook for about ten minutes.
Drain the fish and remove the skin, on plates warmed beforehand in the oven at 80°.
Meanwhile, cook some Creole-style rice or boiled potatoes.
Make the black butter: heat the butter until golden but not burnt (it must not turn black), add a dash of vinegar and the capers and let it simmer.
Plate up and reheat for 30 seconds in the microwave if needed.
Blanch the skate cheeks for 5' in boiling water, drain them and remove any remaining skin.

Melt a large knob of butter in a frying pan and brown the cheeks; cook for 10' over a medium heat, turning the pieces; halfway through, add the tomato cut in half, then the chopped garlic and parsley.
Meanwhile, cook the brown rice in salted water for 13'.
Serve on a warm plate, with a knob of butter on the rice.
Thaw the spinach in the fridge the night before, before going to bed.
In a frying pan, cook the scallops for 5 minutes over a high heat in the white wine and olive oil.
In a bowl, whisk the rest of the crème fraîche, the egg yolks, the chopped chives, salt and pepper. Add 2 tablespoons of the scallops' cooking juice.
Spread the spinach in an ovenproof dish, pour the scallops over it and coat with the egg mixture.
Bake for 20 min in a hot oven (180°) and serve straight from the oven.

notes: Christmas dinner 2023, Foix.

etapes: For the fresh pasta, mix the flour and egg with a fork until perfectly combined.
Then work the dough with your hands until it is smooth and thick.
Then make the fresh pasta with the ATLAS machine. After cutting, leave the pasta to dry on a tea towel.
Thaw the scallops for ½ a day in the fridge, laying them well apart on a plate.
Leave them to marinate for ½ hour in a mixture of ½ milk ½ water.
In a very hot buttered frying pan, cook your (drained) scallops on each side. The scallop should take on a nice golden colour on the outside while staying raw in the middle.
Season, then serve on plates warmed beforehand in the oven at 40°.

notes: Variation: less pasta, but add fresh tomato with slow-cooked shallots.

endives-au-saumon-fume-sauce-bechamel.titre: Chicory with smoked salmon and béchamel sauce

ingredients: 20 g grated Gruyère for the sauce and 10 for sprinkling
etapes: Preheat the oven to gas mark 9.
Wash the chicory and cut it in half lengthways. Steam for 10 to 15 min, then drain carefully.

Make the béchamel sauce in the sauce maker: cook the flour in the butter on setting 3, add the milk, season with salt and pepper, cook for 20' on setting 5; at the end of cooking, add a pinch of ground nutmeg then the Gruyère, keep warm on setting 2.
Roll the chicory in the salmon slices and arrange them in a gratin dish.
Cover with béchamel and sprinkle with Gruyère. Bake in the oven for 15 min. Serve hot.

ingredients: Vinaigrette: olive oil, vinegar, 1 tbsp honey, juice of ½ lemon, salt, pepper
etapes: Rinse and pat dry the salmon fillets, and drizzle them with 2 tbsp of the vinaigrette.
Preheat the oven on “conventional” to 240°, cook the fillets in a dish on the 2nd shelf for about 10', until the flesh flakes easily with a fork; turn them halfway through.
Tear up the salad with half of the remaining vinaigrette and arrange it on the plates.
Place the pears on this bed of greens, then the walnuts and the flaked salmon, still hot.
Pour over the rest of the vinaigrette and serve at once.
Cook the pasta and set aside.
Grill the salmon in a non-stick frying pan, pouring off the melted fat as you go.
In a frying pan over a low heat, put the pieces of salmon and add the crème fraîche, the lemon juice and the pasta. Season the whole thing to taste and stir gently for about 2 min.
On warm plates, serve the tagliatelle with salmon and cream, then sprinkle everything with chopped parsley.

notes: For a special occasion, add orange zest and garnish with 4 fresh basil leaves.

etapes: Lay the salmon steaks flat in a large frying pan with the parsley, lemon peel, peppercorns, bay leaf and a glass of cold water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 10 min, covered.
Meanwhile, mix the egg yolks with the hot water in a bowl over a bain-marie.

If you are using an electric mixer, add the butter in small pieces a little at a time, beating between each addition. Once you have used half the butter, the tricky part of the sauce is over and you can add the rest of the butter more quickly.
Season with salt and pepper and add the lemon juice. You can personalise it by replacing the water with a little white wine and shallot reduction.
Drain the salmon steaks and arrange them on warm plates. Coat them with sauce and serve with boiled potatoes.

notes: Note: there are excellent ready-made hollandaise sauces!! I recommend them!

etapes: Lay the salmon flat in a large frying pan with the parsley, zest, peppercorns, bay leaf and a glass of cold water.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, covered.

Meanwhile, in a bain-marie, whisk the yolks with the hot water, then work in the butter in small pieces, a little at a time, whisking constantly. Once half the butter is incorporated, you can go faster.
Season with salt and pepper and add the lemon juice.
Drain the salmon and serve it on warm plates, coated with sauce, with boiled potatoes.

notes: About 450 calories per person.
Recipe taken from a magazine clipping, retyped as a summary.

saumonette-roussette-a-la-provencale-ou-.intro: Two versions: Provençal-style and à l’armoricaine.

etapes: Cook the dogfish, cut into pieces, for 10 min in a vegetable and white wine court-bouillon. Set aside.
Make the ratatouille: wash the courgettes and aubergine and cut them into medium-sized cubes (plus red and green pepper for those who like it). Cut the tomatoes into quarters and slice the onion.

In a pressure cooker, pour a generous tablespoon of oil and fry the different vegetables one after the other for 5 minutes so that they colour. Start with the peppers, then the aubergines, the courgettes and finally the onions, and finish with the tomatoes.
Mix everything together, season with salt and pepper, add the crushed garlic and the bouquet garni, then cover and cook for 15 minutes once the steam starts.
Before serving, don't hesitate to taste and adjust the seasoning if needed, a pinch of Espelette pepper for example.
Place the dogfish on a dish, add the vegetables, and serve piping hot.
Heat the oil in a sauté pan and sear the dogfish over a high heat for 2 min. Add the chopped shallot and garlic and stir.
Flambé the cognac with a match and pour it into the sauté pan. Gently shake the pan, holding it by the handle, so that all the alcohol burns off.
When all the flames have died down, pour the white wine and the tomato purée into the pan. Add a little salt, pepper, and chilli to taste.
Then add the chervil and tarragon and simmer for 15 min over a low heat.
Place the dogfish on a dish, add the lemon juice and butter to the pan, stir, pour over the dogfish and serve piping hot.
For the spinach: strip the leaves of their very fibrous stalks, wash several times in plenty of water, drain and then blanch the leaves in boiling salted water for 1 minute.
Lift them out and plunge them immediately into iced water to keep their lovely green colour; drain and squeeze the leaves to remove the excess water.
For the fish: tip the sachet of court-bouillon into a litre of cold water and bring to the boil. Cook the dogfish in the boiling water for 10 minutes.
Put the dogfish in a buttered ovenproof dish and add the spinach and crème fraîche. As seen in the photo, I also added the (saved) vegetables from the court-bouillon.
20 minutes before the meal, switch the oven on to 180°. Once it is up to temperature, bake for 10 min.

notes: Note: Skippi loved the court-bouillon vegetables that his mistress didn't want!

ingredients: Optional: capers and a few pitted green olives
etapes: Line a tin with the shortcrust pastry, pricked all over with a fork.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper using the mixer.
Add the fromage blanc, then the flour and finally the grated Gruyère, still beating.
Finally, stir in the drained and flaked tuna.
Pour the mixture onto the pastry.
Put in an oven preheated to 190° on fan setting, on the first shelf.
Bake for 35'.

notes: You can use just a small tin of tuna and make up the rest with surimi.

etapes: Rinse the tuna steaks and set aside.
Wash and peel the carrots, onion and mushrooms. Dice them into a stockpot.
Add the tomato, the seasoning and the olives. Stir. Cook over a medium heat until the vegetables release their water and the onions turn translucent.
Lay the tuna steaks on this mixture, cover and lower the heat.
Simmer for about 20 min.

notes: Serve hot with white rice.
Enjoy your meal.

etapes: In a saucepan, melt the butter and pour in the rice. Once the rice turns translucent, add 2 glasses of salted water and allow 12 minutes' cooking over a low heat from when it comes to the boil.
Cooking the tuna (in oil): 4 min on each side.
Squeeze the lemon juice.
Serve the tuna and rice on warm plates and drizzle with the lemon juice mixed with snipped parsley.

ingredients: 10 cl crème fraîche thinned with half a glass of milk
etapes: Have the fishmonger fillet the trout.
Preheat the fan oven to 230°.
Fry the garlic in a frying pan with the olive oil, then add the almonds and brown them.
Lower the heat, add the crème fraîche diluted in the milk and let it heat for a few moments.
Put the trout fillets in an ovenproof dish and pour the cream and almond mixture over the trout.
Cover the dish with a sheet of foil.
Cook for 30 minutes.

notes: Serve with white rice.

etapes: Gut, scale and flour the trout.
Heat a little oil and 25 g of butter, grill the trout for 5 min on each side and keep them on the warm plates in the oven at 50°. Discard the cooking fat.
Melt the rest of the butter, add the almonds and let them turn golden for 2 min, stirring constantly.
Pour the almonds over the trout with the butter.

notes: Serve with lemon and steamed potatoes.

etapes: Peel the shallots and chop them. Fry them for 3 min in a small covered frying pan, then set aside.
Gut the trout, remove the heads, wash them, wipe them and coat them in flour. Cook them in a frying pan for 3 min on each side. Remove the skin and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°.

Butter an ovenproof dish, put the 2 trout in head to tail, place the shallot between them, add the white wine, chives and parsley, salt, pepper and the lemon juice. Put in the oven for about 10 minutes.
Take the dish out of the oven. Arrange the trout on the plates and put the plates straight into the oven while you reduce the cooking juices and add the crème fraîche.
Coat the trout with the sauce and serve with boiled potatoes.

ingredients: 1 turbot or 1 brill of about 2 kg: have the fishmonger fillet it
For the court-bouillon: 1 leek, 1 carrot, 1 onion, salt, pepper, bay leaf, thyme, parsley
etapes: Remove the zest from one orange, then squeeze the oranges.
Salt the flesh of the fish.
In an ovenproof dish, lay the turbot fillets flesh side down, skin side up, and cover with the court-bouillon, prepared in advance, up to the level of the skin, which should just touch the surface.
Bake at 200° or 210° (depending on the oven) for 20'.

Meanwhile, bring the orange juice to the boil and work in the butter, whisking continuously; add salt, bring back to the boil, add the zest and the cornflour, first mixed with a little cold water, to obtain a smooth sauce.
Serve the fillets on the plates after removing the skin and coat them with the sauce.

notes: Offer the rice separately: the portions of fish being fairly generous.

ingredients: 1 piece of stale bread or some croutons
etapes: Wash and wipe the skate cheeks.
Cook the skate cheeks by covering them with cold water, bring to a simmer, cover, turn off the heat and leave to cook for about ten minutes.
Drain the skate cheeks and remove the cartilage.
Mix the cream with the sliced shallots and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat a dish with a little sauce and sprinkle with a little grated Gruyère. Lay the skate cheeks on top. Spread the toasted bread cubes or croutons over them.
Cover with the rest of the sauce and sprinkle with the rest of the grated Gruyère.
Put in a hot fan oven, 2nd shelf, 210° (gas mark 7), cook for about fifteen minutes and serve quickly on warm plates.
Boil the potatoes in their skins. Peel them, cut them into cubes and brown them in butter.
Brown the chicken thighs and the onions in the oil in the pressure cooker with ¼ litre of champagne. Cook for 10 min.
Dice the Chaource. Melt the cream and the cheese over a low heat; once melted, add the veal stock, season if needed and set aside.
Serve the chicken thighs and the potatoes coated with the sauce.

notes: A salad is always welcome alongside.
Note: if you replace the champagne with a dry white wine, it’s less (festive) but it’s also very good.

etapes: Cut the Savoy ham into thin strips.
Peel the onion and cut it into eight. Fry it in a little neutral oil over a medium heat until translucent.
Add the Savoy ham, then the Savoy white wine and the crème fraîche. Cook over a medium heat for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and season (salt, pepper, grated nutmeg).
Meanwhile, cook the farfalle al dente. When cooked, put them in a gratin dish. Pour the sauce over them and stir.
Cover with grated Beaufort and brown for about 10 minutes in a hot oven.

ingredients: 200 g artisanal green olives, slightly bitter
etapes: Cut the pork into 2 cm cubes and brown them in a casserole with olive oil until the pieces are nicely golden.
Add the sliced onion, the carrots cut into rounds, the mushrooms, the olives and the herbes de Provence.
Pour in white wine (or chicken stock) to cover everything.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer over a low heat for 1 h 30 to 3 h (if you have a real wood fire!!).
5 min before the end of cooking, add the tinned chestnuts.

notes: In a pressure cooker: 40 minutes.

etapes: Peel and slice the onions, then cook them down slowly in a little fat.
Next, peel the potatoes, cut them into slices about 1.5 cm thick and steam them.
Finally, put half of the potatoes in an ovenproof dish, then the smoked herring cut into small pieces, cover with the softened onions and finish with the rest of the potatoes.
Season lightly with pepper and salt. Pour over the cream.
Dot the top of the potatoes with small pieces of butter so that they brown.
Bake in a hot oven at 200° for about 20 min.
